{
  "ssotVersion": "1.9.7",
  "name": "acos-spec-engine",
  "description": "Native ACOS specification engine: structured, dependency-free spec-driven development lifecycle.",
  "lifecycle": {
    "constitution": {
      "id": "constitution",
      "name": "Constitution",
      "description": "Establish project principles, constraints, and authority boundaries before writing specifications.",
      "artifact": "constitution.md",
      "entrypoint": "project.constitution",
      "optional": false
    },
    "specify": {
      "id": "specify",
      "name": "Specify",
      "description": "Convert objectives into a structured spec with stories, requirements, scope, failure modes, and acceptance criteria.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/spec.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.spec"
    },
    "clarify": {
      "id": "clarify",
      "name": "Clarify",
      "description": "Resolve ambiguities, contradictions, and unresolved decisions in the spec before planning.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/spec.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.clarify"
    },
    "plan": {
      "id": "plan",
      "name": "Plan",
      "description": "Produce a dependency-aware implementation plan grounded in repository evidence and the spec.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/plan.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.plan"
    },
    "data-model": {
      "id": "data-model",
      "name": "Data Model",
      "description": "Define entities, relations, invariants, and API contracts implied by the spec and plan.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/data-model.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.datamodel"
    },
    "checklist": {
      "id": "checklist",
      "name": "Checklist",
      "description": "Generate quality checklists for completeness, clarity, consistency, security, and testing.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/checklist.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.checklist"
    },
    "tasks": {
      "id": "tasks",
      "name": "Tasks",
      "description": "Break the plan into actionable, tracked tasks with dependencies, estimates, and owners.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/tasks.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.tasks"
    },
    "analyze": {
      "id": "analyze",
      "name": "Analyze",
      "description": "Cross-artifact consistency analysis: spec, plan, data model, tasks, and checklist must agree.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.analyze"
    },
    "wave-plan": {
      "id": "wave-plan",
      "name": "Wave Plan",
      "description": "Generate a wave-config from structured tasks for parallel agent dispatch.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/wave-config.json",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.execute",
      "optional": true
    },
    "implement": {
      "id": "implement",
      "name": "Implement",
      "description": "Execute the approved tasks with bounded autonomy, updating artifacts as decisions change.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/tasks.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.implement"
    },
    "review": {
      "id": "review",
      "name": "Review",
      "description": "Post-implementation code review for bugs, security, quality, and spec coherence. Produces specs/<feature-id>/review.md.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/review.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.review"
    },
    "tests": {
      "id": "tests",
      "name": "Tests",
      "description": "Detect test framework, generate tests from acceptance criteria, and run them. Produces specs/<feature-id>/tests.md.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/tests.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.tests"
    },
    "lint": {
      "id": "lint",
      "name": "Lint",
      "description": "Detect linter, run it, and auto-fix fixable issues. Produces specs/<feature-id>/lint-report.md.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/lint-report.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.lint"
    },
    "security": {
      "id": "security",
      "name": "Security",
      "description": "STRIDE-driven security review of the implemented change. Produces specs/<feature-id>/security-review.md.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/security-review.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.security"
    },
    "verify": {
      "id": "verify",
      "name": "Verify",
      "description": "Run acceptance criteria, checklists, static checks, and tests independently from implementation.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.verify"
    },
    "converge": {
      "id": "converge",
      "name": "Converge",
      "description": "Gap analysis between spec/plan/tasks and actual implementation before delivery.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/convergence.md",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.converge"
    },
    "ship": {
      "id": "ship",
      "name": "Ship",
      "description": "Prepare the verified change for delivery without assuming publish authority.",
      "artifact": "specs/<feature-id>/",
      "entrypoint": "delivery.ship"
    }
  },
  "featureIdRules": {
    "maxLength": 64,
    "pattern": "^[0-9]{3}-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$",
    "description": "Zero-padded three-digit serial number followed by a short kebab-case name, e.g. '001-native-auth', '042-batch-import'. The same ID is used for the spec directory, branch, and worktree names."
  },
  "branchAndWorktree": {
    "useFeatureId": true,
    "description": "The feature ID is the canonical branch name and worktree directory name."
  },
  "qualityGates": [
    {
      "id": "completeness",
      "name": "Completeness",
      "checks": [
        "Every requirement has an acceptance criterion.",
        "Every acceptance criterion has a verification method.",
        "All known failure modes are documented.",
        "Dependencies and blockers are explicit."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "clarity",
      "name": "Clarity",
      "checks": [
        "User stories name a stakeholder and observable outcome.",
        "No ambiguous pronouns or undefined terms in acceptance criteria.",
        "Scope and non-goals are distinguishable."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "consistency",
      "name": "Consistency",
      "checks": [
        "Spec, plan, data model, tasks, and checklists do not contradict each other.",
        "Terminology matches repository and architecture conventions.",
        "Stable IDs and file references are correct."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "security",
      "name": "Security",
      "checks": [
        "Trust boundaries are identified for every affected surface.",
        "Input validation, auth, and authz are covered.",
        "No credentials or secrets are written to specs or plans."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "tests",
      "name": "Tests",
      "checks": [
        "Each acceptance criterion maps to at least one test or check.",
        "Failure-mode tests are included where practical.",
        "Test commands are recorded and runnable."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "defaultSections": {
    "spec": [
      "user-stories",
      "requirements",
      "scope",
      "non-goals",
      "acceptance-criteria",
      "failure-modes",
      "dependencies",
      "unresolved-decisions"
    ],
    "plan": [
      "summary",
      "phases",
      "milestones",
      "stack-choices",
      "risks",
      "verification",
      "rollback"
    ],
    "data-model": [
      "entities",
      "relations",
      "invariants",
      "api-contracts",
      "migration-notes"
    ],
    "tasks": [
      "overview",
      "task-list",
      "dependencies",
      "estimates",
      "owners"
    ],
    "checklist": [
      "completeness",
      "clarity",
      "consistency",
      "security",
      "tests"
    ],
    "convergence": [
      "summary",
      "gaps",
      "resolved-decisions",
      "unresolved-decisions",
      "delivery-readiness"
    ]
  },
  "lightweightTrack": {
    "description": "A spec may substitute an approved action-plan document for plan+data-model+checklist+tasks. The spec.md MUST declare the lightweight track in its Status field and reference the substituting document. The action-plan document MUST be approved before implementation begins.",
    "substitutedPhases": [
      "plan",
      "data-model",
      "checklist",
      "tasks"
    ],
    "requiredDeclaration": "spec.md Status field must say 'lightweight track — see [document path]'",
    "gate": "The substituting document must be committed and referenced before the implement phase."
  },
  "qualityGatesNote": "qualityGates are textual checks on spec.md (static, pre-implementation). They are orthogonal to the tests/security entrypoints which run executable checks on implemented code (dynamic, post-implementation)."
}

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/0020-resume.md.content:
---
description: Recover project state and continue from the best next action
personalized: true
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

> **Bootstrap note**: If ACOS is not yet installed on this project (no
> `npx acos` available, or `.ssot/` was created by a much older version and
> skills are stale), see `docs/bootstrap.md` for the install + init snippet.
> This skill assumes ACOS is installed and projections are current.

Treat the user's accompanying text as the current objective.

## Project-specific orientation (local-ai-packaged)

`local-ai-packaged` is a Docker Compose–based self-hosted AI stack (Ollama, Open WebUI, n8n,
Flowise, Qdrant, Neo4j, SearXNG, Langfuse, Caddy, and a custom Python MCP server) — an
**infrastructure project, not an application with a test suite**. There is no `npm test` /
`pytest` equivalent to run on resume; treat Docker Compose validity and container health as
the primary "is it working" signal instead.

- **Cheap validity check** (read-only, safe to always run): `docker compose config --quiet`
  (add `-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.minimal.yml` or the other override combination
  named in `.ssot/status.md`/`.ssot/handoff.md` if the session concerns that variant). A
  non-zero exit means the compose graph itself is broken — surface this before anything else.
- **Live health check** (only if containers are expected to be running — do not start the
  stack yourself just to check): `docker compose ps` and `docker ps --filter
  network=ai_network` to see which services are up; do not conclude a service is broken from
  compose config alone.
- **MCP server**: source is `mcp_server/` (Python 3.11, `mcp`/`httpx`/`pydantic`/`starlette`/
  `uvicorn`, built via `Dockerfile.mcp` and `docker-bake.hcl`). If the objective touches it,
  `docker buildx bake --load` rebuilds it; there is no separate unit-test command for it.
- **Registry**: images build to `registry.lan.local:8444/local-ai-packaged/` — do not assume a
  public registry.
- **Ecosystem**: this is a **satellite** of `master-infra` (`.ssot/agents/clients.json` →
  `ecosystemParent.path: ".."`) using the shared external Docker network `ai_network`
  (`laip_ai_network` alias in compose files). Read the parent's `.ssot/status.md` for
  ecosystem-wide state (step 9 below) before assuming this project's Supabase, network, or
  registry setup is self-contained — Supabase is intentionally disabled here in favor of the
  cloud instance provisioned by `archon-v2` (see `.ssot/decisions.md`).
- **`.ssot/agents/runtimes.json`** currently only declares an example `fabric-staging` runtime
  left over from the ACOS template — it does not describe a real runtime for this project.
  Treat step 10 below as a no-op until a real runtime is declared or the stale entry is
  removed; do not run `acos-runtime-sync` against it as if it were live.

## Standard ACOS cycle

The standard ACOS session cycle chains entrypoints to form a complete workflow:

```
Session start:
  0020-resume          → recover state, orient, select next action

During session:
  0040-route           → route to the appropriate entrypoint (spec, migrate, personalize, etc.)
  OR 1840-auto-improve → diagnose → C1 critique → plan → gate → execute → verify

Session end:
  1020-handoff         → status.md + handoff.md + S1 scan + H1 next-cycle-hypothesis.md
  1040-session-bridge  → next-session-prompt.md + copy-paste snippet (thin bridge; mandatory after handoff)

Next session:
  0020-resume          → consumes prompt → launches 1840 (C1 mandatory) → ...
```

Spec: `../acos-mcp-launcher-work/docs/specs/019-cycle-continuity/spec.md` (H1 / C1 / G1 / B1 / X1 / S1 / B2 / E1).

The cycle is **composable**: entrypoints assemble into chains that cover different workflows:

- **Improvement cycle**: `0020 → 1840 → 1020 → 1040 → 0020` (repeat; autocritique each loop)
- **Spec cycle**: `0020 → 0040 → 0100-spec → 0140-plan → 0180-data-model → 0220-checklist → 0260-execute → 0300-verify → 1020`
- **Migration cycle**: `0020 → 0040 → 1100-migrate → 1120-migrate-analyze → 1140-migrate-workflow → 1160-verify → 1020`
- **Personalization cycle**: `0020 → 0040 → 1220-personalize → 1020`

Each entrypoint in a chain knows its successors and predecessors. `1220-personalize` should
specialize the entrypoints in the cycles the project actually uses (Phase 0e of 1220-personalize).

## Cycle intent resolution (before fast-path)

Ordinary ACOS update / version upgrade intent MUST route to `maintenance.rollout` / `0840-rollout` (sole public update door).


Resolve what to launch **before** treating any on-disk bridge as authoritative.
**Intent priority** (highest first):

1. **Current explicit user instruction** — the accompanying text for this turn
   (objective, requested phase, analysis-only / transfer, named consumer, or plain resume).
2. **Explicitly active resume contract** — `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` only when
   qualified as usable (below) **and** not contradicted by (1).
3. **Status / handoff as context** — `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md` inform
   orientation; they do not override (1) or an inactive/contradictory bridge.

### Bridge qualification (mandatory before consume)

Classify `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` before launch:

| State | Meaning | Action |
|-------|---------|--------|
| **absent** | File missing | First cycle / plain resume from user text + status/handoff. Do not invent a bridge. |
| **inactive** | Present but sentinel / collaborative note / empty Action-Objective / explicitly marked inactive | Do **not** auto-launch. Treat as absent; follow current user instruction. |
| **usable** | Complete Action, Consumer, Objective (and expected sections); no contradiction with current instruction | May launch consumer with the **full** contract (**X1** keep-on-disk). |
| **contradictory** | Usable shape, but current user instruction names a different objective, phase, or consumer | Prefer current instruction. Record the conflict; do not silently execute the old bridge. |

Distinguish these scenarios explicitly:

- **Old bridge + new explicit intent** → current intent wins; bridge is context only.
- **Inactive bridge** → ignore for auto-launch; first-cycle or plain resume rules apply.
- **Explicit resume** (user asks to resume / continue the bridge, or pastes the resume snippet without a conflicting objective) → consume usable bridge; keep **X1**.
- **First cycle** (no usable bridge/H1) → launch from user text; degraded H1 input is allowed at C1.

### Requested phase

If the current instruction requests **analysis-only**, **transfer**, diagnose/plan without
implementation, or an equivalent bound: launch the consumer with that phase. The consumer
MUST stop after concrete artifacts (diagnostic, C1, plan, tasks, handoff/transfer) and MUST
NOT implement, commit, push, or implicitly relaunch the next cycle. Analysis is not
authorization to execute. Full execute cycles still require **G1** approve/amend inside
the consumer.

## Fast-path: automated improvement cycle

If the user's intent is to launch an automated improvement cycle (text mentions
"auto-improve", "cycle", or `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` exists),
skip the full drift/diagnostic battery below and fast-path to the cycle:

1. Read `AGENTS.md` for the project's operating contract and conventions (most clients
   auto-load it, but sub-agents and some workflows may not — read it if in doubt).
2. Read `.ssot/handoff.md` and `.ssot/status.md` only (steps 2, 7 below — lightweight).
3. If `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` exists: read the **whole** file (Action, Consumer,
   Objective, Hypothesis, Constraints, Context, Waves, Sub-agents, Resume snippet) —
   not the objective line alone. Launch the consumer (default: `1840-auto-improve`) with that full
   contract. The consumer MUST
   run diagnose + **C1** hypothesis critique before planning and the human gate.
   - **Keep the prompt file after launching the consumer** (**X1**) — it stays on
     disk as the cycle contract for the whole session. `1040-session-bridge`
     deletes the consumed prompt at cycle end, immediately before writing the
     next prompt. Deleting it at launch would lose the contract if the cycle is
     interrupted.
   - **Frontier-consult is optional.** Starting from ACOS 1.9.0, `0200-frontier-consult`
     is NOT invoked automatically by the fast-path. The consumer produces its own plan
     after C1 by default. Frontier-consult is only invoked if the user explicitly requests
     it (e.g. "use a frontier model", or the prompt `## Action` says `--frontier`).
   - If the user explicitly requests frontier-consult: the consumer produces diagnose + C1
     + internal plan first, then launches `0200-frontier-consult --consumer <id>` with the
     objective AND the internal plan as context. The only approval remains G1 inside the
     consumer, then continue with `--from-frontier`.
4. If no session-bridge prompt but the user named a consumer entrypoint (e.g.
   "auto-improve", "1840-auto-improve"): launch that entrypoint directly with the user's
   text as the objective. Do NOT invoke frontier-consult unless the user explicitly asks
   for it.
5. Do NOT run version drift, structural drift, runtime drift, ecosystem drift, or
   handoff-check in fast-path mode — these are background concerns that can run after the
   cycle or on the next plain resume. The cycle is the priority.

The full procedure below runs when the user wants a plain resume (no cycle intent
detected).

## Full procedure

1. Read `.ssot/context-index.md` and `.ssot/specifications.json` to locate active specs and canonical sources.
2. Read `.ssot/handoff.md` for the "Next recommended action" and `.ssot/status.md` for the current objective, active milestone, and open items.
3. Before selecting the next action, verify the project's ACOS version is current:
   1. Read `.ssot/agents/clients.json` and extract `ssotVersion`. If the file does not exist, skip this
      step (the project is not initialized).
   2. Compare with the current ACOS code's `CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION` (from
      `scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs` or the installed ACOS package).
   3. If `ssotVersion < CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION`: **this is a blocker.** Surface it to the user: "Project
      ssotVersion X.Y.Z is older than ACOS version A.B.C. A migration is required before continuing."
      Route to `migration.analyze` / `1120-migrate-analyze` to perform a pre-migration analysis that
      identifies custom content at risk, missing state files, semantic references, and non-conformities
      before the deterministic apply. See `docs/migrations.md` for the full hybrid workflow procedure.
      Do not continue with other resume steps until the migration is complete or the user explicitly
      defers it.
      **After the migration apply completes, always run `npx --no-install acos --fix` to regenerate
      client projections** (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.kilo/`, etc.) from the migrated SSOT. The
      deterministic `acos-migrate --apply` updates canonical sources under `.ssot/` but does not
      regenerate projections itself — that is `acos --fix`'s responsibility. Skipping `acos --fix`
      leaves the project with stale projections that `acos --check` will flag as drift on the next
      resume. Then run `npx --no-install acos --check` to confirm no drift remains.
   4. If `ssotVersion === CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION`: run `npx acos-migrate --root . --reconcile` (dry-run)
      to check for structural drift — the version may match but the file layout may not (manual version
      bumps, partial migrations, custom entrypoint changes). If the reconcile plan reports renames,
      moves, additions, or version bumps, surface them: "Structural drift detected: N changes needed.
      This often indicates the version was bumped with `--bump-ssot-version` without running
      `acos-migrate --apply`. Run `npx acos-migrate --root . --reconcile --apply` to fix." Do not
      continue until the user resolves the drift or explicitly defers it.
      **After `--reconcile --apply` completes, always run `npx --no-install acos --fix` to regenerate
      client projections from the reconciled SSOT.** The reconcile apply updates canonical sources
      but does not regenerate projections. Then run `npx --no-install acos --check` to confirm no
      drift remains. If the user deferred the drift, flag it in `.ssot/handoff.md` so the next resume
      surfaces it again.
      **Also verify `acosSource`**: read `.ssot/agents/clients.json` → `acosSource`. If absent, warn:
      "acosSource not declared in clients.json — ACOS code path must be discovered manually. Consider
      adding acosSource to clients.json." If `type: "local-checkout"` but the path doesn't resolve to
      a valid ACOS checkout (missing `scripts/core/sync-clients.mjs`), warn: "acosSource.path does not
      point to a valid ACOS checkout. Update clients.json or restore the checkout."
   5. If `ssotVersion > CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION`: the ACOS code is outdated. Advise the user: "Project
      ssotVersion X.Y.Z is newer than this ACOS version A.B.C. Update ACOS or roll back the project."
   6. Check for core-reserved slot collisions: if the project has a custom entrypoint at order 1300,
      1320, 1340, 1360, 1380, 1400, 1420, or 1440, surface it as informational (not a blocker): "Custom entrypoint <slug> uses
      order <order>, which is reserved for ACOS core (`1300-mco-relaunch-agent`, `1320-mco-abandon-cycle`,
      `1340-mco-override-dependency`, `1360-mco-prepare-cycle`, `1380-mco-trigger-cycle`, `1400-mco-force-analysis`, `1420-mco-open-pr`, `1440-mco-authorize-merge`). Consider reclassifying or renumbering per
      `docs/specs/000-numbering-conventions/spec.md`." Do not block the resume flow.
   7. **Ecosystem version drift**: if `ecosystemRole === "container"` with `ecosystemChildren`,
      run `npx acos-migrate --root . --reconcile` (dry-run) and check the analysis artifact's
      `ecosystemVersionDrift[]` section. If any satellites are at a different `ssotVersion` than
      the container, surface them: "Ecosystem version drift detected: N satellite(s) are at a
      different version than the container: <satellite-path> (X.Y.Z vs container Z.Y.X).
      Run `npx acos-migrate --root . --ecosystem --apply` to migrate all projects (best-effort, or `--strict` for all-or-nothing with rollback)."
      Do not block the resume flow — this is informational unless the user is about to start
      migration work, in which case it becomes a blocker that must be resolved first.
4. If a specific spec or task is requested, read only that spec's `spec.md` and `tasks.md` rather than all specs.
5. Inspect Git status and recent history without discarding or rewriting existing changes.
6. Run the cheapest useful environment and dependency checks — for this project that is
   `docker compose config --quiet` plus, if containers are expected to be running,
   `docker compose ps` (see "Project-specific orientation" above; there is no test suite to
   run). Use `maintenance.doctor` if drift is suspected and `maintenance.infrastructure` when
   shared platform state matters (note: no `.ssot/infrastructure-profile.json` exists yet, so
   `0680-infra` will report infrastructure as unconfigured — this is expected, not a bug).
7. Compare claimed state with repository evidence and identify stale documentation or incomplete work.
   Use `npx --no-install acos-handoff-check --root .`; if it reports `review` or `stale`, follow its
   recovery evidence before trusting the recorded next action.
8. If the project declares a `gitWorktree` scope in `.ssot/agents/clients.json`, detect the current
   worktree with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Verify the active branch and bare repository against
   the canonical declaration. If the branch mismatches or the bare repository is not at the declared
   path, report it as a blocker and do not continue until the worktree is on the expected branch or the
   declaration is updated.
9. If `.ssot/agents/clients.json` declares an `ecosystemParent`, load the parent SSOT in addition to the
   local SSOT: read the parent `.ssot/status.md`, `.ssot/handoff.md`, and `.ssot/context-index.md`. Merge
   the parent's context with the local context; prefer the local `.ssot` when the same file is declared
   in `ecosystemParent.overridden`.
10. If `.ssot/agents/runtimes.json` exists, read the latest `ACOS_RUNTIME_SYNC_REPORT.json` (if present).
   If the report shows `runtime-diverged`, stop and ask the user to reconcile git and the runtime before
   continuing; offer to run `npx --no-install acos-runtime-sync --root .` to refresh the report. Do not
   run runtime drift/health commands automatically from `0020-resume`.
11. Select the smallest next action that advances the user's objective.
12. **Check for a session-bridge prompt** — if `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` exists, it was
    prepared by `1040-session-bridge` at the end of the previous session. Read the **whole**
    file (Action, Consumer, Objective, Hypothesis, Constraints, Context, Waves,
    Sub-agents, Resume snippet — the snippet section is informational: it is what
    the user pasted to start this session). Show the user the
    consumer, objective, wave synthesis, sub-agent synthesis, and H1 path, then launch
    the consumer. Do not ask "launch now?": the only approval is the consumer's human
    gate (G1).
    - **Default path (no frontier-consult)**: launch the consumer with
      the **full contract**. `1840` must run diagnose + **C1** before plan/gate (**G1** =
      approve/amend only).
    - **Frontier-consult path (opt-in only)**: if the user or prompt requests `--frontier`,
      the consumer produces diagnose + C1 + internal plan first, then
      `0200-frontier-consult --consumer <id>`, then `--from-frontier`. There is no
      separate frontier approval.
    - Keep `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` after the cycle is launched (**X1**) — it
      remains the on-disk cycle contract until `1040` deletes it just before writing
      the new prompt at session end. If the user refuses the later G1 gate, keep the
      file for a future session.
13. Continue directly when intent is clear; ask only when a missing decision materially changes the result. When a question or ambiguity arises, first attempt to resolve it through codebase exploration, documentation, or web research (rule 8). Only ask the user as a last resort, with structured options and justified recommendations.
14. Update durable status and handoff facts after meaningful progress.

Report recovered state, inconsistencies, action taken, and remaining blocker in compact form.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/0040-route.md.content:
---
description: Route a task, specification, or question through the appropriate workflow
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Use the user's accompanying text as the complete request. This is the default single-command
orchestrator for a complete engineering cycle; never require the user to invoke each delivery
entrypoint separately.

1. Classify the request as a question, diagnosis, specification, implementation, verification, or delivery task.
2. Load only the required durable context. If project state is uncertain or stale, apply `project.resume` first without asking the user to repeat the request.
3. For a question or diagnosis, inspect evidence and answer without mutating files unless a fix was also requested.
4. If the task is ambiguous or needs structured refinement, route through the ACOS spec lifecycle: `delivery.spec` (specify/clarify), `delivery.plan`, `delivery.datamodel` (`0180-data-model`), `delivery.checklist`, then `delivery.execute` as needed.
5. For implementation work, apply `delivery.spec` to create or reconcile acceptance criteria, then apply `delivery.plan` to produce a dependency-aware plan grounded in repository evidence.
6. Present the proposed plan and pause for one explicit user approval before the first implementation mutation. Clarifications that materially change scope belong before this approval.
7. After approval, continue the same request autonomously through `delivery.execute`, `delivery.analyze`, and `delivery.verify`. Do not ask the user to re-invoke `0260-execute` or `0300-verify`.
8. After implementation and before verification, run the quality gates: `delivery.review`, `delivery.tests`, `delivery.lint`, and `delivery.security`. Skip a gate if its tool is absent (FM-001). The gate artifacts (`review.md`, `tests.md`, `lint-report.md`, `security-review.md`) feed `delivery.converge`.
9. If verification fails, diagnose and repair in scope, then re-run the relevant verification. Stop only for a product decision, missing authority, or external blocker that cannot be resolved safely.
10. Apply `delivery.converge` before `delivery.ship` to produce a gap analysis and delivery-readiness checklist. The convergence analysis incorporates the quality-gate findings.
11. Apply `delivery.ship` only to prepare delivery. Commit, push, publish, deploy, merge, or external messaging still require explicit authority.
12. Update `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md` after meaningful changes, preserving exact verification evidence and residual risks.

The public invocation remains the numbered client projection (`0040-route`). Internal routing uses
stable semantic IDs and MUST NOT expose an unnumbered replacement command.

## Ecosystem routing

After step 1 (classification), check `.ssot/agents/clients.json` for `ecosystemRole`:

- If `ecosystemRole === "container"` and the task involves **migration** or **version upgrade**: route to `migration.ecosystem` / `1180-migrate-ecosystem` instead of `migration.workflow` / `1140-migrate-workflow`. The ecosystem entrypoint handles batch migration of the container + all satellites. If the task is not migration-related, continue with the normal routing — the container's own SSOT is independent.
- If `ecosystemRole === "satellite"`: proceed normally. The satellite's SSOT is independent. If the task requires ecosystem-wide changes, advise the user to run from the container root instead.
- If `ecosystemRole === "standalone"` or absent: proceed normally. No ecosystem routing needed.

## Non-spec routing

Not all tasks go through the spec lifecycle. After classification (step 1), route these task types to their dedicated entrypoints.

**Intent priority** (same rule as `0020-resume`): current explicit user instruction →
explicitly active resume contract → status/handoff as context. Qualify
`.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` as absent, inactive, usable, or contradictory before
treating it as cycle intent. Mere file presence does **not** override a different
explicit request.

- **Migration or version upgrade**: route to `project.migrate` / `1100-migrate` (the migration router). The router determines whether it's a new install, version upgrade, or reconciliation, and dispatches to `1120-migrate-analyze`, `1140-migrate-workflow`, or `1180-migrate-ecosystem` as needed.
- **Personalization**: if the user asks to personalize, customize, or specialize the SSOT for the project (e.g. "customize entrypoints for my stack", "personalize ACOS for this project"), route to `project.personalize` / `1220-personalize`.
- **Auto-improve cycle**: if the user's text names auto-improve / cycle / `1840`, or a
  **usable** (non-contradictory) `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` is selected under intent
  priority, route to `project.resume` / `0020-resume` which handles the fast-path launch
  of `project.autoimprove` / `1840-auto-improve`. Pass any **requested phase**
  (including analysis-only / transfer): analysis produces artifacts and stops without
  implicit implementation, commit, or relaunch.
- **Session end / handoff**: if the user wants to end the session or write a handoff, route to `session.handoff` / `1020-handoff`.
- **Next session preparation**: if the user wants to prepare the next session's auto-improve cycle, route to `session.bridge` / `1040-session-bridge`.
- **Git operations**: route to `git.layout` / `0500-git-layout`, `git.acp` / `0540-git-acp`, `git.pr` / `0580-git-pr`, or `git.cleanup` / `0620-git-cleanup` as appropriate.
- **Doctor / drift diagnosis**: route to `maintenance.doctor` / `0640-doctor`.
- **Projection sync**: route to `maintenance.sync` / `0660-sync`.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/0200-frontier-c.content:
---
description: Frontier-grade strategic analysis — the current client answers in-session by default; --cli opts into cross-model dispatch
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Produce a frontier-grade analysis on a question, plan, or approach that the current agent
cannot resolve confidently alone. **The agent running this entrypoint IS the frontier
consultant.** When this entrypoint executes inside Codex, Codex answers; inside Claude,
Claude answers; the same for every ACOS client. The analysis happens in-session — no other
client CLI is spawned by default. The frontier consultant does NOT create a plan from
scratch; it validates, critiques, and improves an existing plan produced by the primary
agent (or by the consumer entrypoint when `--consumer` is set).

## When to use this

- The current agent is stuck or uncertain about an architectural decision.
- A refactor/migration deserves a deeper analysis pass before execution.
- A plan needs adversarial review before execution.
- The user explicitly asks for a frontier model's opinion — or explicitly wants a second
  opinion from a DIFFERENT client/model family (`--cli`).

## Execution modes — `self` is the default

- **`self` (default)**: the current session's client performs the frontier analysis itself.
  No CLI dispatch, no spawned agent session, no sub-agent playing the role — the client the
  user invoked this entrypoint under IS the consultee. Running a second client would add a
  hop without adding independence the user asked for.
  - `--model` is advisory in self mode: an agent cannot switch its own model mid-session.
    If the requested model differs from the one running the session, say so in one line and
    either proceed with the current model or ask whether the user wants an external dispatch
    (`--cli`) instead.
  - Self mode answers with the session's own model. If you want a stronger or different
    model family to weigh in, the user must pass `--cli <client>` explicitly.
- **external (`--cli <name>`)**: explicit opt-in — dispatch the question to a DIFFERENT
  client CLI for a cross-model second opinion (e.g. the session runs under Codex but the
  user wants Claude's take). Use only when `--cli` is passed or the user unambiguously asks
  for another client ("get Claude's opinion", "ask Devin"). `--cli` naming the SAME client
  as the current session is meaningful only combined with `--model <other>` — invoke that
  client's headless mode with `-m/--model <model>` as a raw one-shot prompt, never as an
  entrypoint run.

### Anti-recursion — hard rule

A dispatched consult is **terminal**: the spawned session answers, it never re-dispatches.
This is the fix for the "double frontier consult" failure mode: the spawned client used to
load the project's ACOS harness, pattern-match its task onto this skill, and spawn yet
another client.

- Every externally dispatched prompt file MUST begin with the consultation marker below,
  and the spawned session's first message (interactive mode) MUST repeat it.
- **Consultee detection**: if the request you are processing contains the marker
  `ACOS-FRONTIER-CONSULTEE`, YOU are the consultee. Do NOT execute this entrypoint (or any
  ACOS entrypoint/skill), do NOT spawn another CLI/agent/sub-agent, and do NOT modify the
  project. Read the question and context under the marker and answer directly.

```text
ACOS-FRONTIER-CONSULTEE — You are the consulted frontier model. Answer the question below
directly with your own analysis. Do NOT invoke any ACOS entrypoint or skill (including
0200-frontier-consult), do NOT dispatch to another agent or CLI, do NOT spawn sub-agents,
and do NOT modify the project. One-shot consultation: read the context, think, answer.
```

## Philosophy — read this before building the prompt

**The frontier consultant is a smarter peer, not an instruction follower.** Whether the
consultee is this session (self) or a dispatched client (external), its value is reasoning
capacity — if you tell it exactly what to do, you waste that capacity and get nothing of
value. The whole point is an **independent critical analysis** that a cheaper pass cannot
produce.

**The primary pattern**: a cheaper pass (Tier 1/2) produces a detailed plan → the frontier
consultant (Tier 3) critiques, validates, or restructures it. Send the plan + the context +
the objective, and ask "is this plan sound? what would you change?". Do NOT send a
step-by-step specification of what the answer should look like.

**Do**: give the consultant the objective, the project context, the relevant files, and the
plan/approach to review. Clear variables, clear constraints, clear question.

**Don't**: inject your own analysis, tell it what the answer should be, assign it a role, or
dictate output format (unless `--consumer` is set). If you tell it what to think, it will
react to your hypothesis instead of forming its own. The anti-recursion marker above is the
ONLY fixed directive — it is a routing guard, not an answer constraint.

## Tier routing and budget gate (mandatory)

This entrypoint is **Tier 3 (Premium)** by intent — it buys a deeper analysis pass:

- **Never start here.** Tier 1 (Auto/Cascade) and Tier 2 (Named Models) MUST be attempted
  first for the task at hand. Frontier-consult is escalation only — use it after a cheaper
  pass has failed or when the user explicitly requests it.
- **Direct invocation = approval.** When the user explicitly invokes this entrypoint (e.g.
  `/0200-frontier-consult ...`), that invocation IS the authorization. Do NOT ask "are you
  sure?" — announce in one line which mode will be used (self, or which CLI/model for
  external), then proceed. No gate.
- **Subagent usage.** If this entrypoint is invoked from a subagent (not a top-level user
  session), the subagent MUST obtain explicit prior approval from the user before running
  it — self or external. Subagents cannot authorize quota consumption on their own. This is
  the ONLY case where you stop and ask.
- **Token budget.** Self mode consumes the session's own model quota; external mode consumes
  the dispatched client's quota on top. If the user has declared a token budget (in
  `.ssot/status.md` or verbally), track consumption and warn when the consult would exceed
  the remaining budget. If no budget is declared, proceed without warning.

## Inputs

The user's accompanying text is the **question**. Optionally:
- `--files <path1,path2,...>` — files to include as context (read and appended).
- `--model <name>` — target frontier model. Advisory in self mode (you cannot switch your
  own model); applied to the spawned CLI in external mode. Do not guess model names — see
  the "Orchestrator / frontier model policy" below (canonical), and
  `docs/model-selection.md` / `docs/agent-waves/model-selection.md` where present, or ask
  the user.
- `--cli <name>` — dispatch to a different ACOS client CLI (default: `self`). See
  "Available CLIs" below.
- `--consumer <entrypoint-id>` — format the consultant's plan output for direct consumption
  by the named entrypoint. See "Consumer-aware mode" below.

## Available CLIs (external dispatch reference — used only with `--cli`)

The following ACOS clients have a CLI suitable for external dispatch. The table is the
**complete and canonical reference** — binary, Windows absolute path, prompt mode, output
mode, and the **mandatory bypass approvals + sandbox flag**. Use the bypass flag in EVERY
external invocation (interactive AND headless) so the CLI never pauses to ask for approval.

| CLI | Binary | Windows absolute path | Prompt mode | Output mode | Bypass flag (MANDATORY — use every time) |
|-----|--------|-----------------------|-------------|-------------|------------------------------------------|
| Claude Code | `claude` | `%APPDATA%\npm\claude.cmd` | file (`--prompt-file`) | stdout (`-p`) | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` |
| OpenAI Codex | `codex` | `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd` | positional or stdin (`codex exec - `) | stdout | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` |
| Devin CLI | `devin` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\devin\cli\bin\devin.exe` | file (`--prompt-file`) | export-log (`--export`) | `--permission-mode dangerous` |
| Cursor | `agent` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent\agent.cmd` | positional (no `--prompt-file`) | stream-json | `--force` (alias `--yolo`) + `--trust` |
| Kilo Code | `kilocode` | `%APPDATA%\npm\kilocode.cmd` | positional (`--command`) | stdout | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (or `--auto`) |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | `%APPDATA%\npm\opencode.cmd` | file (`--prompt-file`) | stdout | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` |

> **Bypass flag is MANDATORY in every external invocation.** Without it, the CLI pauses on
> every tool call asking for approval — the user has to accept commands constantly. Always
> include the bypass flag from the table above, whether interactive or headless.

### Binary discovery — mandatory procedure (do NOT skip to invocation)

**On Windows, `Get-Command <cli>` / `command -v <cli>` FAILS for most CLIs even when they are
installed.** npm global bins (`%APPDATA%\npm\`) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent\` are
typically NOT in the agent's PATH. You MUST probe the absolute fallback paths. Do not
conclude a CLI is "not installed" just because `Get-Command` returned nothing.

Follow this 3-tier discovery in order. Stop at the first tier that resolves a usable binary:

**Tier 1 — PATH lookup (fast but unreliable on Windows):**
```powershell
Get-Command claude,codex,devin,agent,kilocode,opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Select-Object Name, Source
```
On Linux/macOS: `command -v claude codex devin agent kilocode opencode 2>/dev/null`

**Tier 2 — Windows absolute path probe (mandatory when Tier 1 finds nothing):**
```powershell
$candidates = @{
  claude    = @("$env:APPDATA\npm\claude.cmd")
  codex     = @("$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.cmd", "$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.ps1")
  devin     = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\devin\cli\bin\devin.exe")
  agent     = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cursor-agent\agent.cmd")
  kilocode  = @("$env:APPDATA\npm\kilocode.cmd")
  opencode  = @("$env:APPDATA\npm\opencode.cmd")
}
foreach ($cli in $candidates.Keys) {
  foreach ($p in $candidates[$cli]) {
    if (Test-Path $p) { Write-Output "FOUND: $cli -> $p"; break }
  }
}
```
Use the resolved absolute path as the binary for invocation (e.g. `& "$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.cmd"
exec ...` instead of `codex exec ...`).

**Tier 3 — project overlay (machine-specific paths):**
If the project has an agent-waves overlay file (e.g. `docs/agent-waves-overlay-<project>.md`),
read it for the machine-specific `DEVIN_BIN`, `CURSOR_BIN`, `OPENCODE_BIN` variables. These
override the Tier 2 defaults when present.

**If all three tiers fail for a CLI**: that CLI is genuinely not installed. Report it to the
user with the install command (see links below) and fall back to self mode — do NOT silently
chain to yet another client.

### Model selection — read before choosing a model

The golden rule: **invest in thinking (expensive models), save on execution (free/cheap
models).** This entrypoint is Tier 3 — for external dispatch you want a planning-grade
model, not an execution-grade one. But the user may override.

#### Orchestrator / frontier model policy (OpenAI GPT-6 — Oct 2026)

When dispatching to Codex (or whenever an OpenAI model is the consultee), the canonical
orchestrator chain is:

```
                gpt-6.1-sol (reasoning effort: high → xhigh)
                    ORCHESTRATEUR
                         │
      critique / architecture / synthèse / décomposition
                         │
          ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
          ▼              ▼              ▼
     gpt-6-luna     gpt-6-luna     gpt-6-luna      sous-agents (recherche, exécution, analyse)
          └──────────────┼──────────────┘
                         ▼
               résultats compacts → gpt-6.1-sol (synthèse / décision)
```

- **`gpt-6.1-sol`** is the primary frontier model ($2/M input, $10/M output; ~1.05M
  context, 128K max output) for plan critique, architectural reasoning, decomposition,
  dependency analysis, enrichment, and planning waves of sub-agents.
- **`reasoning.effort`: `high` by default** (API default is `medium`; scale is
  `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`). Use `xhigh` for difficult architectural decisions or
  conflicting constraints, `max` for final review of high-stakes plans. `none`/`minimal`
  are NOT supported on `gpt-6.1-sol`/`gpt-6-astra` (`gpt-6-luna` supports them). Codex
  CLI: `-m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`.
- **Context target ≤ 200K input tokens per request** — a per-request size target, not a
  cumulative task/token budget. Before approaching 200K, compact older context while
  preserving requirements, decisions, unresolved issues, architecture, constraints, and
  the references downstream agents need.
- **Avoid crossing 272K input tokens** unless the extra context is genuinely necessary:
  above 272K, OpenAI applies long-context pricing to the ENTIRE request, cached input
  included (2× input & cache rates, 1.5× output).
- **Exploit prompt caching**: keep stable instructions/context at the front of the
  prompt; avoid unnecessary changes to the shared prefix.
- **`gpt-6-luna`** ($0.10/M in, $0.50/M out — ~20× cheaper than Sol) is the default
  sub-agent model: targeted, high-volume tasks that return concise findings to the
  orchestrator. Never burn the frontier model on routine execution that can be
  delegated.
- **`gpt-6-astra`** ($10/M in, $50/M out — 5× Sol) is escalation-only: exceptionally
  difficult synthesis/reasoning where Sol's result is demonstrably insufficient.
- **`gpt-5.6-*` is previous-generation and currently costs MORE than `gpt-6.1-sol`**
  (`gpt-5.6-sol`: $4/M in, $20/M out). Do not select 5.6 for new work.

Quick reference (canonical — do not guess model names):

| Use case | Model class | Examples (API ID) |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| **Architecture, migration strategy, critical analysis** | Frontier orchestrator | `claude-opus-5-5`, `gpt-6.1-sol` (effort `high` → `xhigh`) |
| **Exceptional synthesis — escalation only** | Top-tier | `claude-fable-5-1`, `gpt-6-astra` |
| **Standard planning, spec review, capture d'essence** | 2nd-tier planning | `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gpt-6.1-sol` (effort `high`) |
| **Execution of already-planned tasks / sub-agents** | Free/economic | `gpt-6-luna`, `kimi-k2-7` ; sous-agents Devin CLI `run_subagent` = **`swe-2`** — **jamais Haiku, jamais GPT-5.x** |

**Do not guess model names.** If unsure, ask the user which model to use rather than
inventing an API ID. Model names change frequently; the table above is the canonical
reference embedded in this entrypoint.

### Launch modes (external dispatch only)

- **Interactive** (default for external consults): visible in a terminal pane (Windows
  Terminal `wt.exe` or `tmux` on Linux/WSL) for human supervision. **The spawned session
  MUST receive the consult as its first message** — pass the marker plus the prompt-file
  path as the initial prompt (positional argument where the client supports it), so the
  consultee reads the prompt file itself. Never launch a bare interactive session and assume
  the prompt arrives some other way: a session that starts empty cannot consult.
- **Headless** (opt-in, for automated pipelines only): non-interactive, captures
  stdout/export-log to a file. Used by `wave-dispatch.mjs --mode cli-headless` and when the
  consultant's output is consumed by another entrypoint (`--consumer` mode) without human
  review. **Do not use headless as the default for external consults** — it hides the
  consultant's reasoning from the user.

For interactive mode, wrap the invocation in `wt new-tab` (Windows) or `tmux new-session`
(Linux/WSL). The wrappers below pass the marker + prompt-file pointer as the initial
message and include the bypass flag.

**Windows Terminal interactive wrappers (copy-paste ready — marker + prompt-file pointer + bypass flag in every one):**

```powershell
$promptFile = "docs\prompts\<timestamp>-<cli>-<slug>.md"   # written in the procedure below
$brief = "ACOS-FRONTIER-CONSULTEE — read '$promptFile' in this directory and answer it directly per the marker instructions."

# Claude Code — interactive + bypass + initial prompt (positional)
wt new-tab --title "Claude" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "chcp 65001 >nul & & '%APPDATA%\npm\claude.cmd' --model claude-opus-5-5 --dangerously-skip-permissions `"$brief`""

# Codex — interactive + bypass + initial prompt (positional; no subcommand = TUI)
wt new-tab --title "Codex" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "chcp 65001 >nul & & '%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd' -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust `"$brief`""

# Devin CLI — interactive + bypass (--prompt-file delivers the prompt file directly)
$devin = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\devin\cli\bin\devin.exe"
wt new-tab --title "Devin" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "& '$devin' --model kimi-k2-7 --permission-mode dangerous --prompt-file '$promptFile' --export '$stage\export.jsonl'"

# Cursor agent — interactive + bypass (positional initial prompt, --force + --trust)
wt new-tab --title "Cursor" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "& '$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cursor-agent\agent.cmd' `"$brief`" --force --trust --workspace $workdir"

# Kilocode — interactive + bypass (start the session, then paste $brief as the first message)
wt new-tab --title "Kilocode" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "chcp 65001 >nul & & '%APPDATA%\npm\kilocode.cmd' --dangerously-skip-permissions"

# OpenCode — interactive + bypass (start the session, then paste $brief as the first message)
wt new-tab --title "OpenCode" --startingDirectory "$workdir" `
  cmd /k "chcp 65001 >nul & & '%APPDATA%\npm\opencode.cmd' --dangerously-skip-permissions"
```

For clients without a positional initial prompt (Kilocode, OpenCode), the launching agent
MUST instruct the user (one line) to paste `$brief` as the first message, or use headless
mode instead. What matters is that the marker + prompt-file path reach the consultee.

**Headless wrappers with bypass approvals + sandbox (for `--consumer` mode, wave-dispatch, automated pipelines — absolute paths):**

The prompt FILE already begins with the `ACOS-FRONTIER-CONSULTEE` marker (see "Build the
prompt" in the procedure), so headless delivery needs no extra framing:

```powershell
# Claude Code — headless + bypass
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\claude.cmd" --model claude-opus-5-5 --dangerously-skip-permissions -p < prompt.md

# Codex — headless + bypass
Get-Content prompt.md | & "$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.cmd" exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -

# Devin CLI — headless + bypass (dangerous mode = auto-approve all tools)
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\devin\cli\bin\devin.exe" --model kimi-k2-7 --permission-mode dangerous --prompt-file prompt.md --export export.jsonl

# Cursor agent — headless + bypass (--force = auto-approve, --trust = skip workspace trust)
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cursor-agent\agent.cmd" -p --force --trust --model auto --output-format stream-json --workspace $workdir < prompt.md

# Kilocode — headless + bypass
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\kilocode.cmd" run --command "<name>" --dir $workdir --dangerously-skip-permissions

# OpenCode — headless + bypass
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\opencode.cmd" run --dangerously-skip-permissions < prompt.md
```

> **Codex interactive vs headless**: `codex` (no subcommand) = interactive TUI — the default
> for external dispatch. `codex exec` = non-interactive (headless, opt-in only for automated
> pipelines or `--consumer` mode). Both accept `-m <model>`. For unattended headless:
> `codex exec -m <model> --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<prompt>"` or pipe via
> stdin: `Get-Content prompt.md | codex exec -m <model> --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -`.

> **Bypass approvals + sandbox — MANDATORY in every external invocation (interactive AND
> headless).**
> - Claude: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
> - Codex: `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (+ `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` to skip the ACOS Stop hook)
> - Devin: `--permission-mode dangerous` (or `smart` — fast-model safety classifier; auto-approves
>   routine dev work but still prompts for destructive ops, package installs, and sensitive paths —
>   a middle ground when full bypass feels too broad for a supervised consult)
> - Cursor: `--force` (alias `--yolo`) + `--trust`
> - Kilocode: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (or `--auto`)
> - OpenCode: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
>
> Never omit the bypass flag, even in interactive mode. The user supervises the reasoning in
> the pane but should NOT have to approve every tool call.

**Not listed**: Gemini CLI. Gemini is not an ACOS client (not in the 7 required clients). If
a user explicitly requests Gemini, it MAY be used as a non-client external tool, but it is
not a default and should not be presented as an ACOS channel.

If no ACOS client CLI is available for an explicitly requested external dispatch, fall back
to self mode and say so — do NOT silently chain to yet another client. Install links:
- `claude`: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code
- `codex`: https://github.com/openai/codex
- `devin`: https://devin.ai/cli
- `agent` (Cursor): `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex` (Windows) or
  `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsSL | bash` (Linux/macOS)
- `kilocode`: `npm install -g @kilocode/cli`
- `opencode`: https://dev.opencode.ai/

## Consumer-aware mode (`--consumer <entrypoint-id>`)

When `--consumer <entrypoint-id>` is provided, the consultant's plan is structured for
direct consumption by the named entrypoint. This enables the pattern: **consumer entrypoint
produces a draft plan (cheap) → frontier consultant critiques and improves it (Tier 3) →
consumer entrypoint executes the improved plan (cheap)**. Consumer mode works in BOTH
execution modes — self (the current agent produces the improved plan) and external (the
dispatched client produces it).

**The calling entrypoint MUST provide its draft plan as context for critique.** The
consultant's role is to validate, critique, and improve an existing plan — NOT to create one
from scratch. If the calling entrypoint sends only the objective without a draft plan, the
frontier pass is wasted (it produces a plan the cheaper model could have produced itself).
The draft plan should be included via `--files` or as part of the prompt context.

### How it works

1. **Resolve the consumer entrypoint**: look up `<entrypoint-id>` in `.ssot/agents/workflows.json`
   (by stable ID or source filename), then read the corresponding file in
   `.ssot/agents/entrypoints/`.
2. **Read the `planConsumer` section from its frontmatter**: if present, it contains:
   - `specPath` — where to persist the plan (e.g. `"specs/auto-improve-{date}/"`)
   - `planFile` — the filename (e.g. `"tasks.md"`)
   - `planFormat` — the exact format the consumer expects (a YAML multi-line string)
   - `{date}` is replaced with today's date (YYYY-MM-DD).
3. **If no `planConsumer` section**: fall back to the default advisory format and warn the
   user that the consumer entrypoint does not declare a plan consumer.
4. **If `planConsumer` is present**: add the planFormat to the analysis as a format
   constraint on the plan section only (see the procedure).
5. **After the analysis** (self or external): in addition to
   `docs/prompts/<timestamp>-...-output.md`, persist the plan to `<specPath>/<planFile>`
   (creating directories as needed).
6. **Gate**: present the plan to the user for approval. After approval, hand off to the
   consumer entrypoint. The consumer detects the pre-existing plan file and skips its own
   planning phases — this is the consumer's responsibility to implement (typically via a
   `--from-frontier` flag or by checking if the plan file already exists).

### What the consumer declares (project-specific, not ACOS source)

The consumer entrypoint's frontmatter is project-owned. ACOS source does not hardcode any
consumer. Any entrypoint (ACOS source or project custom) can declare a `planConsumer` section:

```yaml
planConsumer:
  specPath: "specs/auto-improve-{date}/"
  planFile: "tasks.md"
  planFormat: |
    - [ ] **T-001** — <description>
      - Depends on: none
      - Files: `<path>`
      - Domain: code|tests|docs|infra
      - Parallelizable: true|false
      - Lane: A1
```

The `planFormat` is injected verbatim into the consult (self: your own analysis contract;
external: the dispatched prompt). The consumer is responsible for parsing and executing the
plan file it receives.

## Procedure

1. **Resolve the execution mode** — `self` unless the user passed `--cli <name>` or
   unambiguously asked for another client. If `--cli` names the SAME client as the current
   session, it only makes sense with `--model <other>` (same-client different-model
   headless dispatch); otherwise treat it as `self` and say so in one line. You do not need
   to detect which client hosts the session — `self` is correct by definition.

2. **Announce and proceed** — state in one line what will happen (e.g. "Self-consult —
   analyzing in-session" or "External consult via Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) with 3 context
   files..."), then proceed immediately. **Do NOT ask for approval** — the user's invocation
   of this entrypoint is the approval. The only exception is subagent invocation (see "Tier
   routing and budget gate" above), which requires explicit prior user approval.

3. **Gather context** — the most important step. The quality of the analysis depends almost
   entirely on the quality of the context.

   - **Read the project context**: `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`,
     `.ssot/handoff.md`. If the question is architectural, also read `.ssot/constitution.md`
     and `.ssot/architecture.md`. If a feature ID is active, read the active
     `spec.md`/`plan.md`/`tasks.md`.
   - **Select relevant files**: if `--files` provided, use those. If not, select the files
     most relevant to the question (max 5 by default; prefer `.ssot/` canonical sources over
     generated projections; summarize files >500 lines instead of including full content).
     Exclude files matching `.env*`, `*credential*`, `*secret*`, `*token*` (see Authority).
   - **Do NOT inject your own hypotheses about the answer.** The point of the consult is an
     independent-style analysis. Provide the question and the context — let the frontier
     pass do the thinking.

4. **Self path (default)** — produce the analysis yourself, at full depth:

   - Apply the philosophy above: critique, validate, restructure. Answer the question
     directly in your response.
   - Persist the analysis to `docs/prompts/<timestamp>-self-<slug>-output.md` for the audit
     trail (`<timestamp>` = UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ`, `<slug>` = short kebab-case question
     label). No prompt file is written — there is no dispatch.
   - Continue at step 6.

5. **External path (`--cli` only)** — dispatch to the requested client:

   a. **Detect the CLI** — follow the 3-tier "Binary discovery" procedure above. If the
      requested CLI is not found after all 3 tiers, fall back to self mode and tell the
      user (do NOT chain to a different client on your own initiative).
   b. **Build the prompt file** — `docs/prompts/<timestamp>-<cli>-<slug>.md`. Content:

      ```text
      ACOS-FRONTIER-CONSULTEE — You are the consulted frontier model. Answer the question
      below directly with your own analysis. Do NOT invoke any ACOS entrypoint or skill
      (including 0200-frontier-consult), do NOT dispatch to another agent or CLI, do NOT
      spawn sub-agents, and do NOT modify the project. One-shot consultation: read the
      context, think, answer.

      ---

      <the user's question, verbatim>

      ---

      ## Project context

      <relevant sections of context-index.md, status.md, handoff.md, architecture.md, etc.>

      ## Files

      <file contents, each under a ## File: <path> heading>
      ```

      The marker is the ONLY fixed directive — it prevents the spawned session (which loads
      this project's ACOS harness and sees this skill) from re-dispatching the consult.
      Beyond it: no role assignment, no output contract, no budget lectures.
      **If `--consumer` was provided and a `planConsumer` section was found**, add one line
      after the question: `Produce the plan section in this exact format (it will be
      consumed by <entrypoint-id>):` followed by the planFormat.
   c. **Persist the prompt path** — state `docs/prompts/<timestamp>-<cli>-<slug>.md` in one
      line so the user can review it. Do NOT block waiting for review.
   d. **Invoke** — interactive mode (default) via `wt new-tab`/`tmux` with the marker +
      prompt-file pointer as the session's first message (wrappers above); or headless when
      `--consumer` is set / the user asks for it, capturing stdout to
      `docs/prompts/<timestamp>-<cli>-<slug>-output.md`. In interactive mode, save the output
      to the same path when the session ends.

6. **Present the answer** — self: your analysis is already the answer. External: read the
   output file and present the consultant's answer.
   **If `--consumer` was NOT provided**: this is a standalone consultation. Present the
   answer. Do not execute anything — the user decides what to do with the advice.
   **If `--consumer` was provided**: the plan is an intermediate artifact. The consumer
   entrypoint (e.g. `1840-auto-improve`) will generate the final wave-config and present IT
   for approval (that is the single human gate). Do NOT pause here — hand off immediately to
   the consumer entrypoint (e.g. `/devin:<consumer-id> --from-frontier`). The consumer
   detects the pre-existing plan file and skips its own diagnostic/planning phases.

7. **Persist the artifact** — if a feature ID is active, also write a copy of the analysis
   to `specs/<feature-id>/frontier-consult-<timestamp>.md` (or `docs/specs/<feature-id>/` if
   that is the project's spec location). Otherwise keep the output in `docs/prompts/`.
   The persisted artifact MUST include: the mode (self/external), the client and model, the
   timestamp, and the full response (plus the prompt file path when dispatched externally).
   **If `--consumer` was provided and a `planConsumer` section was found**: additionally
   persist the plan to `<specPath>/<planFile>` (creating directories as needed). This is the
   file the consumer entrypoint will read to execute the plan.

8. **No cleanup** — do not delete the prompt or output files. Both are persisted in
   `docs/prompts/` for auditability and reproducibility.

## Authority

- This entrypoint is **read-only** — it produces analysis text. In self mode it reads files
  and writes only the persisted artifact (and the consumer plan file when `--consumer` is
  set); it does not mutate project code. In external mode the dispatched CLI is constrained
  by the marker to the same read-only contract.
- The consultant's output is advisory. The current agent does not execute the plan.
  In standalone mode (no `--consumer`), the user decides what to do with the advice. In
  `--consumer` mode, the consumer entrypoint generates the final wave plan and presents
  THAT for approval — the frontier output is an intermediate artifact, not the approval
  point.
- Do not send secrets, credentials, or `.env` contents into the analysis. If `--files`
  includes a file that looks like it contains secrets (`.env*`, `*credential*`, `*secret*`,
  `*token*`), stop and ask the user before including it.

## Relationship to agent waves

This entrypoint MAY be used as a single-agent wave step (per `docs/agent-waves/04-RUNBOOK.md`).
When used inside a wave:
- The wave-config generator MUST mark this step as `tier: 3` and `quota-consuming: true`.
- The wave MUST obtain user approval before executing this step (this is the subagent case —
  wave steps are not direct user invocations, so the budget gate applies).
- A wave step runs in self mode unless the wave config explicitly requests `--cli` — a lane
  must never silently dispatch to another client.
- The output file path MUST be recorded in the wave status JSON so downstream agents can read
  the consultant's recommendation.
- This entrypoint MUST NOT be parallelized with itself in the same wave (one frontier
  invocation at a time to control cost).

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/0780-docker.md.content:
---
description: Docker compose lifecycle with mutation gates
personalized: true
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Manage the project's Docker compose lifecycle.

**Project-specific compose layout (local-ai-packaged)**: this project ships six compose files,
not one — `docker-compose.yml` (base, 15+ services: Ollama, Open WebUI, n8n, Flowise, Qdrant,
Neo4j, SearXNG, Langfuse + backing services, Caddy), `docker-compose.minimal.yml` (reduced
footprint override), `docker-compose.override.yml`, `docker-compose.override.private.yml`,
`docker-compose.override.public.yml`, and `docker-compose.override.public.supabase.yml`
(Supabase is disabled by default — the project uses a cloud instance from `archon-v2`; only
compose it in deliberately). Always ask or infer from `.ssot/status.md`/`.ssot/handoff.md`
which combination applies before running `-f` chains — `docker compose config --quiet` against
the wrong combination silently validates the wrong graph. The custom MCP server image
(`Dockerfile.mcp`) builds via `docker buildx bake --load` (`docker-bake.hcl`), not `docker
compose build`. Services join the external network `ai_network` (`laip_ai_network` alias) —
`docker network create ai_network` must exist first if starting fresh; `start_services.py`
wraps the common startup sequence.

1. Detect `docker-compose.yml` or `compose.yaml` in the project root. If neither exists, skip with a note.
2. Determine the requested action from the user's prompt:
   - **Read-only** (no mutation gate): `logs`, `health` (healthcheck status), `config validate` (`docker compose config --quiet`).
   - **Mutating** (requires explicit user confirmation): `up`, `down`, `rebuild`, `restart`.
3. For mutating actions, state exactly what will run and wait for explicit user approval before executing. Never run `up` or `rebuild` without confirmation.
4. For read-only actions, run directly and report output.
5. Boundary with `maintenance.infrastructure` (`0680-infra`): that entrypoint discovers **external** read-only infrastructure (LAN hosts, remote Docker). This entrypoint manages the **project's own** compose stack. Do not confuse the two.
6. Produce a summary of the action taken, containers affected, and their health status.
7. Do not push images, deploy to registries, or touch external infrastructure — those require `delivery.ship` authority.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/0840-rollout.md.content:
---
description: Update ACOS in an initialized project or an explicitly scoped batch; inspect first, then run only the required projection, structural, and semantic work
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Treat the user's accompanying text as the update objective. Minimize questions.

## Public update contract

**All ordinary requests to update an already-initialized ACOS project enter through
`maintenance.rollout` / `0840-rollout`.** Migration entrypoints (`1100`/`1120`/`1140`/
`1160`/`1180`/`1240`) are **internal phases** or **compatibility paths** — not a menu the
operator chooses from.

- **Default scope**: the named project / current root only. Being a container does **not**
  expand scope to satellites.
- **Explicit batch**: registry path or ecosystem scope must list every target and carry
  through planning and approval.
- **Uninitialized projects** (no `.ssot/agents/`): do **not** use this entrypoint — route to
  `project.migrate` / `1100-migrate` (install/adopt).
- **Engine**: discover via `acosSource`. Do **not** `git pull` / `npm install` unless the
  user explicitly authorized an engine update.

### Personalized skills — spirit of the method (mandatory)

`personalized: true` in the **frontmatter** is only the **flag**. What is personalized is the
**body** (the skill text). The flag tells the engine “do not wholesale-replace this file”.

When ACOS improves a **template** entrypoint, that improvement must be **recovered into the body**
of every personalized twin. Different wording from the template is **expected**. That difference
is **not** proof the project is up to date.

**Rule:** each personalized body must still carry **at least** the template’s current
directives, structure, rules, gates, and must-do steps. Project-specific content stays; missing
template obligations are **merged into the body** by the agent (best fit, not a blind paste).

**Wrong:** “Bodies differ → skip / ok.”  
**Wrong:** overwrite the personalized file with the raw template.  
**Wrong:** treat classification `needsMigrate` (B) as “no C needed”.  
**Right:** template = baseline obligations; personalized body = baseline + project specifics.
**Order:** unfinished work runs **A → B → C** as needed (B first when structure lags; C always
when personalized files exist).

Rollout is **not complete** while any personalized entrypoint lacks obligations present in the
matching template source under the engine’s `templates/ssot/.ssot/agents/entrypoints/`.

### C handoff (when semantic work is needed)

Before calling an internal semantic phase, prepare a handoff with:

- target root, engine/target version, evidence paths, findings summary
- already completed steps (e.g. B apply done)
- allowed files / write-set for the delta (every personalized entrypoint that lags the template)
- for each file: **template obligations to recover** (checklist) + what to preserve
- requested phase (`analysis-only` | `focused-delta` | `full-hybrid`)
- approval scope already granted

**C can exist at equal versions.** Pending C means rollout is **not** complete. `--apply` on
rollout authorizes only the reviewed structural/projection scope — analysis-only never mutates.

## Purpose

Classify from **evidence** (version, structural, projection, semantic). A/B/C are
**intervention levels that may combine** — not an exclusive pipeline and not “always 1140”.

| Level / class | Meaning | Tooling |
|---------------|---------|---------|
| **A — `needsFixOnly`** | Projections may drift; version current | `acos --fix` + `acos --check` |
| **B — `needsMigrate`** | Version behind and/or missing structural pieces | `acos-migrate` plan → gate → `--apply` → A |
| **C — `needsSemanticAgent`** | Personalized / contract-body / refs | **Focused** `1140` delta or `1240` — not full hybrid by default |
| **`blocked`** | Unreadable clients, newer-than-engine, etc. | Stop — never report as `ok` |

MUST stop a project's mutation chain after a failed migrate/fix prerequisite. Version bump
+ `--fix` alone does **not** prove current cycle semantics if entrypoint bodies are stale.
CLI classify is a **preflight**, not proof of all body drift — use reviewed reconcile tooling
when structure/body findings remain. See `docs/acos-rollout.md`.

**Symlink / `local-checkout` is the preferred engine supply.**

## Inputs

- Optional `--registry <path>` — explicit multi-project batch.
- Optional `--root <project>` — single project (default: current workspace).
- Optional `--apply` — user must approve before apply; without it, classify + dry-run only.
- Optional ecosystem scope — only when the user explicitly names container+satellites.

## Procedure

### 1. Resolve ACOS engine

1. Read `.ssot/agents/clients.json` → `acosSource`.
2. If `local-checkout`: resolve path; confirm `CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION`. No pull unless asked.
3. If `npm`: confirm installed package matches intended release; update only when asked.

### 2. Classify (deterministic)

```bash
node <acos>/scripts/lifecycle/acos-rollout.mjs --root <project> [--registry ...]
```

Interpretation:

- Version behind → **B** (then A); personalized risk → flag **C** after B.
- Version equal + missing contract/perso findings → **C** and/or **A**.
- Version equal + clean → **A** or done.
- Blocked / newer-than-engine → stop.

### 3. Execute by class

**A — fix only**

```bash
node <acos>/scripts/core/sync-clients.mjs --root <project> --fix
node <acos>/scripts/core/sync-clients.mjs --root <project> --check
```

**B — migrate (structure first; then C if personalized)**

1. Dry-run migrate plan; present plan + class report (`levels` may be `B+C+A`).
2. Before `--apply`: ensure `.ssot/migration-analysis.json` matches this from→to
   (`scannerVersion` = engine, `review.status=complete`, contentHashes fresh). If stale:
   run the analysis scanner for from→to, complete the review dispositions, then apply.
3. On approve: `--apply`, then **A**, then **C** when `levels` includes C (audit FAIL).
4. Stop the chain on migrate/fix failure.
5. Never tell the user “done at B” while personalized obligations audit fails.
6. Engine refuses `apply-ok` until personalized obligations audit PASS (Spec 022).

**C — semantic (bounded) — personalized merge**

1. Run (or read from rollout report) `acos-personalized-audit` — **mechanical proof** of
   missing obligation IDs. Do not invent a write-set from memory alone.
2. Optional: `acos-rollout … --emit-c-handoff` → `.session/rollout-c-handoff.json`.
3. For each file in `writeSet`: read template twin; merge **missing obligation IDs** into
   the personalized body (keep project text; no wholesale template replace).
4. Prefer `1140-migrate-workflow` **Mode 1 — Focused semantic delta** (equal version OK).
5. Full five-phase `1140` **only** if the user explicitly asked for full hybrid.
6. Use `1240-migrate-refs` only when refs findings + opt-in authority exist.
7. Re-run `acos-personalized-audit` until PASS; then final A/check.
8. **Audit FAIL or `*-semantic-pending` ⇒ not success** (never claim done).

### 4. Audits / verify

```bash
node <acos>/scripts/audit/model-routing-audit.mjs --root <project>
node <acos>/scripts/audit/personalized-obligations-audit.mjs --root <project>
```

Optionally `1160-migration-verify` with the mode matching available evidence.

### 5. Persist

Update `.ssot/status.md` / `.ssot/handoff.md`: class, versions, C pending or done, next action.

## Authority

- No commit / push / runtime-sync.
- No **wholesale replace** of `personalized: true` bodies with the template file.
- **Do** merge template obligations into personalized bodies (agent judgment) when templates
  advanced — that is required work, not optional polish.
- Batch / ecosystem apply requires explicit user approval for `--apply`.
- Do not skip personalized files merely because the CLI classifier did not list them; the
  template↔perso obligation check above is part of 0840.

## Related (internal)

- `1100-migrate` — install/adopt only; initialized updates redirect here
- `1140-migrate-workflow` — focused C delta or explicit full hybrid
- `1120` / `1160` / `1180` / `1240` — internal phases
- `docs/acos-rollout.md`

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1020-handoff.md.content:
---
description: Persist a factual end-of-session handoff
personalized: true
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Update `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md`. Record completed work, exact current state, modified files, verification results, unresolved problems, next recommended action, and commands needed to resume. Separate facts from assumptions. Do not claim completion when required checks failed or were not run. Flag any unresolved questions that were researched but could not be resolved — include what was investigated and what remains unclear so the next session can pick up the research (rule 8).

**Project-specific verification (local-ai-packaged)**: this is an infrastructure project with
no test suite — do not report "tests passed" as a verification. Instead, run and record the
result of `docker compose config --quiet` (add the override files relevant to the session,
e.g. `-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.minimal.yml`) before claiming a compose or
Dockerfile change is verified. If a container was touched, also record whether it was
restarted and observed healthy (`docker compose ps`), not merely that the config parses.

When the session involved a material decision between options, record the alternatives considered, their impacts, and why the chosen option was selected (decision-support rule) — this feeds the next cycle's C1 critique.

If the canonical context sources under `.ssot/agents/context/` (e.g., `AGENTS.src.md`, `CLAUDE.src.md`) were edited during the session, run `npx --no-install acos --fix` (or `maintenance.sync` / `0660-sync`) so the generated projections (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and client-specific pointers) are regenerated before handing off. Do not edit generated projections directly.

Run `npx --no-install acos --check` to confirm projections are in sync, then run
`npx --no-install acos-handoff-check --root .` to verify handoff/git consistency. Reconcile any
Git state/count contradiction before ending the session; do not edit the handoff automatically
merely to increase its score. Since spec 019 **E1**, the same check also verifies the
session bridge on a fresh handoff (`.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` + H1 artifact) —
run `1040-session-bridge` before this check or it will flag the gap.

After the handoff is written, check `.ssot/agents/dependencies.json`.
