   This confirms the post-merge agent (`1240-migrate-refs`) performed a real content merge on each `personalizedDrift` entry (see "Personalized entrypoint merge" in `docs/migrations.md`) instead of skipping it or blindly adopting the template. Flag any entrypoint still listed in `personalizedDrift` with no corresponding merge evidence as a verification failure.
8. If gaps are found, propose concrete next actions:
   - analysis-driven: re-apply the missing resolution (e.g. re-run `acos-migrate --apply` if a `resolutionStrategy: "add"` entrypoint is still absent), or revise the analysis artifact's `resolutionStrategy` if the operator's intent changed;
   - legacy-backup: migrate an unmapped legacy file; archive it and record a decision; delete an orphaned current file if it is no longer needed.
   - missing surface: re-run `acos --fix` to regenerate the missing projection, or verify `clients.json` declares the projection if it is still absent.
   - missing banner: re-run `acos --fix` to regenerate the file with the correct `legacy` or `desktopOnly` banner.
9. Do not mutate the project autonomously. Pause for explicit approval before any fix.
10. After fixes, re-run the verifier in the same mode until the report passes.
11. Update the target project's `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md` with the verification outcome.
12. **Handoff**: after verification is complete (all checks PASS), launch `1020-handoff` to persist the session state. This closes the migration chain (`0020 → 0040 → 1100 → 1120 → 1140 → 1160 → 1020`). If verification FAILS and the user chooses to roll back, do not launch 1020 — instead surface the rollback path (see `1140-migrate-workflow` → "Rollback per phase") and wait for user direction.

## Upstream producers

This entrypoint consumes artifacts produced by:
- **`1120-migrate-analyze`** — produces `.ssot/migration-analysis.json` (the analysis artifact with `projectionGaps` and `resolutionStrategy` fields).
- **`1140-migrate-workflow`** — orchestrates the full 5-phase migration and delegates Phase 4 verification to this entrypoint.

If neither producer has been invoked, the analysis artifact will be absent and verification falls back to legacy-backup mode (if `.ssot.legacy/` exists) or reports "nothing to verify against".

## Completion checklist

Before declaring verification complete, verify:

- [ ] ACOS code is current (version check output shown)
- [ ] Verification mode selected (analysis-driven OR legacy-backup) and justified
- [ ] `migration-verify.mjs` was run (show full output)
- [ ] All projection surfaces verified (Devin, Codex, Kilo, OpenCode, Cursor, Claude)
- [ ] Legacy banners present on `legacy: true` projections
- [ ] Desktop-only banners present on `desktopOnly: true` projections
- [ ] If `personalizedDrift[]` present in the analysis artifact: `--check-post-agent-diff` run and each entry confirmed merged
- [ ] If gaps found: concrete next actions proposed
- [ ] If gaps fixed: re-run verifier until PASS
- [ ] **Final step verification** — `migration-step-verify.mjs` run and reports PASS (show output)

**This entrypoint verifies but does NOT mutate.** If gaps are found, propose fixes but do not
apply them without explicit approval.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1180-migrate-ec.content:
---
description: Migrate a container project and all its satellites to a target ssotVersion in a best-effort batch (use --strict for all-or-nothing with rollback) — batch migration with per-project status reporting
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Treat the user's accompanying text as the migration objective. Minimize questions.

## ⚠️ Autonomy directive — READ BEFORE PROCEEDING

You are an autonomous agent performing an ecosystem migration (container + satellites).
**You decide, you don't ask.**

- **DO**: Analyze each project in the ecosystem, identify drift, resolve duplicates, decide
  migration order, and handle per-project non-conformities yourself.
- **DO**: Resolve version drift by migrating to the target version. Resolve duplicate entrypoints
  by choosing the correct one. Handle missing/unreadable satellites by documenting them and
  proceeding with the rest.
- **DO NOT**: Ask the user per-item questions. Present the complete ecosystem migration plan at
  Gate 1 (all projects, all versions, all drift), get a single approval, then execute.
- **ASK THE USER ONLY**: When a satellite is genuinely broken in a way you cannot fix (e.g.
  corrupted JSON you can't parse, or a business decision about whether to include/exclude a
  satellite from the ecosystem).

## Prerequisites

1. Identify the container project root from the user's request. If not provided, ask for it.
2. Verify the project is a **container**: read `.ssot/agents/clients.json` and check `ecosystemRole === "container"` with a non-empty `ecosystemChildren` array.
   - If the project is standalone or a satellite, stop and direct the user to `1120-migrate-analyze` / `1140-migrate-workflow` for single-project migration.
3. **⚠️ CRITICAL — Verify the installed ACOS code is up to date.** The migration engine runs from the ACOS code in `node_modules/@acos/core` (npm) or `acosSource.path` (local-checkout). If this code is stale, the batch migration uses old logic and will fail or produce incorrect results across all satellites. Before proceeding:
   - Read `acosSource` from `clients.json`. If `type: "npm"`, run `npm install --save-dev git+https://github.com/oues81/acos.git#main` to update. If `type: "local-checkout"`, verify the source repo is at the latest commit (`git -C <path> pull`) and that `node -e "console.log(require('<path>/scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs').CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION)"` matches the target version.
   - **Never run `acos-migrate --ecosystem --apply` with stale ACOS code.** Changing the version number in `package.json` or `clients.json` does NOT update the code — the actual scripts, schemas, and templates must be replaced.
   - If the user provides an ACOS source path, use that path to verify the version. Do not assume `node_modules` is current.
4. Resolve the ACOS code path: read `acosSource` from `clients.json`. If `type: "npm"`, use `<project-root>/node_modules/@acos/core`. If `type: "local-checkout"`, resolve `acosSource.path` relative to the project root. If absent or invalid, ask the user.

## Phase 0 — Ecosystem audit (read-only)

1. Run the pre-migration analysis scanner on the container:
   - `node <acos-path>/scripts/core/migration-analysis.mjs <container-root> --from=<current> --to=<target>`
2. Review the `ecosystemVersionDrift[]` section in the generated `.ssot/migration-analysis.json`:
   - For each satellite with `status: "drift"`, note the current and target versions.
   - For each satellite with `status: "missing"` or `status: "unreadable"`, flag it — it will be skipped during batch migration.
3. For each satellite, run the analysis scanner individually to generate per-project analysis artifacts:
   - `node <acos-path>/scripts/core/migration-analysis.mjs <satellite-root> --from=<current> --to=<target>`
4. Review all analysis artifacts for non-conformities (`malformedJson`, `versionMismatch`, `versionBumpedWithoutMigration`, etc.). Critical non-conformities must be resolved before proceeding.
5. **Ecosystem gate check**: for each satellite, verify whether the ecosystem gate is open. The gate is open when `clients.json` has `ecosystemParent.path` starting with `ecosystem-parents/`, the named manifest exists in the ACOS template, and the profile file exists at the manifest's declared path. If the gate is closed, ecosystem-category entrypoints (13xx–14xx) will be skipped during migration with `resolutionStrategy: "skip"` — the verifier will not flag their absence as a failure.

## Gate 1 — Ecosystem migration approval

Present a concise summary to the user:
- Number of projects in the ecosystem (container + N satellites).
- Current versions vs target version for each project.
- Any non-conformities or drift findings.
- Satellites that will be skipped (missing/unreadable).
- The migration order: container first, then satellites in sequence.

Pause for explicit approval before proceeding.

## Phase 1 — Batch migration

1. Run the batch migration:
   - Dry-run first: `node <acos-path>/scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs --root <container-root> --ecosystem --target <target-version>`
   - Review the per-project plan output.
   - If approved, apply: `node <acos-path>/scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs --root <container-root> --ecosystem --target <target-version> --apply`
2. The batch migration:
   - Migrates the container first (full structural migration + version bump + projection regeneration).
   - Migrates each satellite in sequence (same apply logic, individually).
   - If a satellite migration fails, remaining satellites are still attempted (best-effort).
   - Prints a summary report with per-project status (`migrated` / `failed` / `skipped`).

## Gate 2 — Post-migration review

1. Review the batch migration report:
   - Check that all projects succeeded (`allSucceeded: true`).
   - If any failed, surface the error and advise the user to fix the failing project individually using `1140-migrate-workflow`.
2. Run `acos --check` on each project to verify no drift remains:
   - `npx --no-install acos --root <project-root> --check`
3. Verify `acosSource` propagation: for each satellite, check that `acosSource` is present in `clients.json`. If absent, run `npx --no-install acos --root <satellite-root> --fix` to trigger inheritance from the container.

## Phase 2 — Post-migration cleanup

1. For each migrated project, update `.ssot/status.md` with the new `ssotVersion` and migration completion status.
2. Update `.ssot/handoff.md` with the next recommended action.
3. Record all durable decisions in the container's `.ssot/decisions.md`.

## Completion

Report to the user:
- Number of projects migrated successfully.
- Any failures or skipped projects.
- The new ecosystem-wide `ssotVersion`.
- Recommended next action (e.g., `acos --check` on each project, or commit and push).

Never mutate any project before explicit approval. Never run `--ecosystem --apply` without a prior dry-run review. The container must always be migrated before satellites.

## Ecosystem structure — what you need to know

Each project in the ecosystem (container + satellites) has its **own independent `.ssot/`**.
The ecosystem relationship only controls:

- **`acosSource` sharing**: satellites inherit the container's ACOS code path automatically.
  Satellites do NOT need their own `node_modules` or `@acos/core` install.
- **`inherited` files**: canonical files copied from container to satellite at each `acos --fix`.
  Edits to inherited files in the satellite are overwritten — list them in `overridden` instead.
- **`overridden` files**: files the satellite manages itself (not propagated from container).

A satellite with `inherited: []` is 100% independent — it only shares `acosSource`. See
`1100-migrate.md` → "Ecosystem setup" for the full setup procedure and configuration examples.

## Completion checklist (MANDATORY)

Before declaring the ecosystem migration complete, verify each item for EACH project (container
+ every satellite). **Show the output of each command — do not claim success without proof.**

- [ ] **ACOS code updated** — `CURRENT_SSOT_VERSION` matches target
- [ ] **Phase 0 audit** — analysis run on container AND each satellite
- [ ] **Ecosystem gate check** — each satellite's gate status verified
- [ ] **Gate 1 passed** — user approved the ecosystem migration plan
- [ ] **Dry-run reviewed** — `--ecosystem` (no `--apply`) output shown to user
- [ ] **Batch apply** — `acos-migrate --ecosystem --apply` run (show per-project status)
- [ ] **Post-migration check** — `acos --check` run on EACH project (show outputs)
- [ ] **acosSource propagation** — each satellite has `acosSource` in `clients.json`
- [ ] **Final verification** — `migration-step-verify.mjs` run on EACH project (show outputs)
- [ ] `.ssot/decisions.md` updated (in container) with migration decision
- [ ] `.ssot/status.md` + `.ssot/handoff.md` updated for EACH project

If any project fails verification, the ecosystem migration is NOT complete. Report which
projects passed and which failed with their specific gaps.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1220-personaliz.content:
---
description: Analyze an initialized ACOS project and personalize its SSOT items based on the project's actual codebase, architecture, conventions, and current client best practices
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Treat the user's accompanying text as the personalization objective. Minimize questions.

## Overview

This entrypoint orchestrates the SSOT personalization feature (spec 009). It follows a hybrid
agent + deterministic model where **the agent leads understanding and the script leads mechanics**:

- **Agent layer** (this entrypoint): deep codebase reading, project comprehension, needs
  identification, client-surface gap analysis, semantic judgment on which recommendations
  are relevant, human-approval gate interaction, and decision-logging narrative. The agent
  reads the actual code, understands what the project does, identifies what the SSOT is
  missing or gets wrong, and proposes improvements grounded in that understanding.
- **Deterministic layer** (the script `scripts/audit/ssot-personalization.mjs`): codebase
  scanning, stack detection, architecture classification, SSOT item reading, recommendation
  structuring, report generation, apply/rollback, decision logging. All mechanical, reproducible,
  offline. No network, no LLM. The script is a **complement** to the agent's understanding —
  it catches what the agent might miss mechanically, but it does not replace semantic judgment.

The agent never writes canonical SSOT sources directly — it calls the script's
`applyRecommendations()` function, which is deterministic.

## Procedure

### Phase 0 — Deep project understanding (agent, read-only)

Before any analysis or recommendations, the agent must **understand the project as a
developer would**. This is not optional — without this, personalization is generic noise.

#### 0a. Read the codebase

Read the project's actual source files — not just `.ssot/` metadata. At minimum:

- The entry point(s): `package.json` scripts, `pyproject.toml` entry points, `main.*`,
  `__main__.py`, `index.*`, or equivalent.
- The core modules: read the 3–5 most important source files that implement the project's
  primary logic. Use `grep`/`glob` to find them if not obvious.
- The test files: understand what is tested and how.
- The config files: `.env.example`, `config.*`, `*.yaml`, `*.toml` — understand the
  runtime configuration surface.
- The build/deploy files: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.*`, CI configs, Makefile.

#### 0b. Understand what the project does

Form a mental model and write it down internally:

- **Purpose**: What does this project do? Who uses it? What problem does it solve?
- **Architecture**: How is the code organized? What are the main modules and how do they
  interact? Is it a library, a CLI, a service, a pipeline, a satellite in an ecosystem?
- **Stack**: Language(s), frameworks, key dependencies, database, external services.
- **Conventions**: Naming, error handling, logging, testing patterns, commit style.
- **Ecosystem role**: Is this a standalone project, a container, or a satellite? Does it
  have a parent? Children? Siblings it coordinates with?
- **Active state**: What is the current objective (from `.ssot/status.md`)? What is blocking
  or in progress (from `.ssot/handoff.md`)?

#### 0c. Understand the existing SSOT and client surfaces

Read and assess every SSOT item against what you now know about the project:

- **`.ssot/agents/context/AGENTS.src.md`** — Does it accurately describe the project? Is the
  architecture section correct? Are the conventions real or template boilerplate? Are there
  project-specific constraints (auth patterns, external services, data flows) that are missing?
- **`.ssot/agents/rules/common.md`** — Are the rules relevant to this project? Are there rules
  that contradict the project's actual conventions? Are there project-specific rules that
  should exist but don't (e.g. Fabric auth, SQL patterns, API contracts)?
- **`.ssot/agents/clients.json`** — Which clients are configured? Are the projections correct?
  Are there clients configured that the project doesn't use? Are there clients the project
  uses but that aren't configured?
- **`.ssot/protected-paths.json`** — Are the protected paths accurate? Are there project-specific
  files that should be protected but aren't?
- **`.ssot/constitution.md`** — Does the constitution reflect the project's actual principles
  and constraints? Or is it generic template text?
- **Entrypoints** — Read the custom entrypoints (order ≥600 or IDs with project-specific
  prefixes). Do they describe real workflows that match the codebase? Are there workflows
  the project actually needs that don't have entrypoints? Are there entrypoints that describe
  obsolete workflows?

For each client surface (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.devin/`, `.kilo/`, `.opencode/`, `.codex/`):
- Read the projected skills, rules, and config.
- Assess: does this projection give an agent working in this client enough context to be
  productive? What's missing? What's misleading?

#### 0d. Identify needs and gaps

Based on 0a–0c, write down:

1. **What the SSOT gets right** — items that accurately reflect the project. Don't touch these.
2. **What the SSOT gets wrong** — items that contradict the actual codebase or are stale
   template boilerplate that doesn't apply. These need correction.
3. **What the SSOT is missing** — project-specific knowledge, rules, context, or entrypoints
   that would make an agent more effective but don't exist. These need addition.
4. **Client surface gaps** — for each client, what would make the projection more useful?
   Missing skills? Rules that don't project correctly? Config that's wrong for the project's
   actual tooling?

This needs assessment is the **primary input** to personalization. The deterministic script
is a secondary input that catches mechanical gaps the agent might overlook.

#### 0e. Identify active entrypoint cycles

Understand which entrypoint cycles the project actually uses. The standard ACOS cycle is:

```
0020-resume → 1840-auto-improve → 1020-handoff → 1040-session-bridge → (next session) 0020-resume
```

Check:
- Does the project use the auto-improve cycle? (Look for `.session/` artifacts, references to
  `1840-auto-improve` in decisions or handoff.)
- Does the project use the spec engine cycle? (`0100-spec → 0140-plan → 0180-data-model → 0220-checklist → 0260-execute → 0300-verify`)
- Does the project have custom cycles? (Custom entrypoints at 1500+ that chain together.)
- Which entrypoints in these cycles have generic/boilerplate content that should be personalized?

**Prioritize personalization of entrypoints in active cycles.** An entrypoint that is part of a
daily cycle (0020, 1840, 1020, 1040) has more impact than one that is rarely invoked.

---

### Phase 1 — Deterministic analysis (complement to Phase 0)

Run the deterministic analysis script to produce a structured `ProjectAnalysis`:

```
npx acos-personalize --root . --json
```

If the user passes `--focus <csv>`, forward it to limit analysis categories (valid values:
`context`, `rules`, `clients`, `entrypoints`, `constitution`). If the user passes `--dry-run`,
note it — no files will be modified.

If the script exits with code 2 (FM-001 — not ACOS-initialized), direct the user to `0000-new`
or `1100-migrate` and stop.

**Merge the script's findings with your Phase 0 needs assessment.** The script catches
mechanical issues (stack detection, schema validation, missing fields). Your Phase 0 assessment
catches semantic issues (wrong descriptions, missing project-specific rules, stale context).
Both matter. Deduplicate where they overlap.

### Phase 1b — Personalization planning (agent)

Before generating the report, prioritize the merged findings into a structured plan:

1. **Sort by impact on active cycles** (Phase 0e):
   - **Priority 1**: auto-improve cycle entrypoints (0020, 1840, 1020, 1040) — these entrypoints
     are invoked every session.
   - **Priority 2**: context and rules (AGENTS.src.md, common.md) — affect all agents.
   - **Priority 3**: clients.json and protected-paths — affect projections.
   - **Priority 4**: constitution and other entrypoints — less frequently invoked.

2. **Group by category** (context, rules, clients, entrypoints, constitution):
   - Each group can be approved/rejected independently at Phase 4.
   - A group should not exceed 5-7 recommendations to keep the approval gate manageable.

3. **Identify dependencies**:
   - If a recommendation on `AGENTS.src.md` affects projections, note that `acos --fix` is
     needed after.
   - If a recommendation modifies an entrypoint body, note that `personalized: true` must be
     added to the frontmatter (Phase 5).

4. **Estimate scope**:
   - **Light**: 1-3 files, no risk of breaking projections.
   - **Medium**: 4-10 files, requires `acos --fix` after.
   - **Heavy**: >10 files or structural modifications — split into sub-groups.

This planning structures the report (Phase 3) and the approval gate (Phase 4) into prioritized
and manageable groups rather than a flat list.

---

### Phase 2 — Client best-practices research (agent layer)

If `--refresh-best-practices` was requested, or if any client's best-practices cache is stale
(older than 90 days) or missing, use `web_search` to research current best practices for each
of the 7 required clients:

- **Claude Code** (`claude`) — search for current Claude Code skills, rules, hooks, and MCP config
  patterns.
- **Cursor** (`cursor`) — search for current Cursor rules, commands, skills, and hooks patterns.
- **Devin** (`devin`) — search for current Devin CLI skills, config, and hooks patterns.
- **Kilo Code** (`kilocode`) — search for current Kilo Code skills, commands, workflows, and rules.
- **OpenCode** (`opencode`) — search for current OpenCode commands, skills, rules, and agents.
- **OpenAI Codex** (`codex`) — search for current Codex agents, hooks, and config patterns.
- **Eve** (`eve`) — search for current Eve agent instructions, skills, connections, hooks, tools,
  and subagent patterns.

Write the refreshed cache to `docs/client-best-practices/<client>.md` with frontmatter
(`client`, `lastResearched`, `sourceUrls[]`) and a body of structured best practices. The cache
ships with the ACOS npm package as a shared baseline; consumer projects override locally.

If web search fails for a client, keep the existing cache and mark it `stale: true` (FM-002).
Do not crash — graceful degradation.

**Cross-reference best practices with your Phase 0 client-surface assessment.** A best practice
is only a recommendation if it's relevant to this project. Don't propose a Docker skill for a
project that has no Dockerfile. Don't propose a Cursor hook for a project where the team uses
Devin. Filter by what you learned in Phase 0.

---

### Phase 3 — Present the report

Generate `ACOS_PERSONALIZATION_REPORT.md` at the project root. The report must include:

1. **Project understanding summary** — what the project does, its architecture, its stack,
   its ecosystem role. This proves the agent read the code and isn't generating generic noise.
2. **Needs assessment** — the 4 categories from Phase 0d (right, wrong, missing, client gaps),
   with specific file references and concrete descriptions of what's off.
3. **Deterministic findings** — the script's mechanical findings, merged with the needs assessment.
4. **Client best-practices gaps** — only the ones relevant to this project (filtered by Phase 0).
5. **Proposed changes grouped by category** — each proposal must reference the specific need it
   addresses. No generic "add a rule about testing" — instead "add a rule about pytest fixture
   scope because the project uses session-scoped fixtures in tests/conftest.py and the current
   rules don't mention it."

---

### Phase 4 — Approval gate

Present the proposed changes grouped by category and ask the user to approve or reject each
group (or all/none). The approval structure is:

```
{ approved: Recommendation[], rejected: Recommendation[] }
```

- **FM-006** (all rejected): write the report with "no changes applied" and exit cleanly.
- Recommendations with `conflictsWith` set (contradicting an existing `D-xxx` decision) are
  automatically excluded from the apply step and noted in the report (FM-003).
  `checkDecisionConflicts()` parses `.ssot/decisions.md`, extracts prohibition patterns
  ("MUST NOT X", "no X", "never X") from each decision, and marks recommendations whose
  `proposed` text affirmatively proposes a prohibited term.
- Recommendations with `preservesCustomization: true` are automatically skipped and noted in the
  report (INV-004).

---

### Phase 5 — Apply approved changes

For each approved recommendation, call the script's `applyRecommendations(approved, root)`
function. This:

- Modifies **only** canonical SSOT sources (INV-003 whitelist): `.ssot/agents/context/*.src.md`,
  `.ssot/agents/rules/common.md`, `.ssot/agents/clients.json`, `.ssot/protected-paths.json`,
  `.ssot/constitution.md`, and entrypoint files.
- Takes an in-memory backup before any write.
- Never edits projection files directly.

**Personalization marker**: When a recommendation modifies the **body** of an entrypoint file
(not just its frontmatter description), add `personalized: true` to that entrypoint's frontmatter.
This marker tells the reconcile engine that the **entire entrypoint** (body + frontmatter description)
has been intentionally customized and should not be overwritten by `acos-migrate --reconcile --apply
--refresh-bodies`. The marker protects both the body and the description from template-driven refresh.

To remove the marker (e.g. when a personalization is no longer needed), use:
```
npx acos-migrate --root . --reconcile --apply --unpersonalize <entrypoint-source>
```

Example — before personalization:
```yaml
---
description: ...
---
```

After personalization:
```yaml
---
description: ...
personalized: true
---
```

Only add the marker when the **body** is modified. A frontmatter-only description update
does not warrant the marker. The marker is optional and backward-compatible: entrypoints
without it are treated as non-personalized (eligible for body refresh via `--refresh-bodies`).

---

### Phase 6 — Regenerate projections

After all approved mutations, run `acos --fix` to regenerate projections. If `acos --fix` fails
(FM-004), the script rolls back all canonical-source changes from the in-memory backup and
reports the failure with error output. Do not proceed if rollback occurred.

---

### Phase 7 — Log decisions

For each applied recommendation, the script appends a `D-xxx` entry to `.ssot/decisions.md`
with the recommendation ID, category, file, section, rationale, and `appliedAt` timestamp. Use
the next available D number.

---

### Phase 8 — Update report

Update `ACOS_PERSONALIZATION_REPORT.md` with the applied status for each recommendation.

---

### Phase 9 — Gitignore the report (first run only)

On first run, add `ACOS_PERSONALIZATION_REPORT.md` to the project's `.gitignore` (or create one
if none exists). The report is a transient artifact (DD-009-007); durable decisions are in
`.ssot/decisions.md`.

## Personalizing the auto-improve cycle (0020 → 1840 → 1020 → 1040)

The auto-improve cycle is the primary ACOS use case. Here is how to personalize each
entrypoint in the cycle:

### 0020-resume

- **Diagnostic commands**: replace generic commands with the project's actual commands
  (tests, build, lint, scan).
- **Ecosystem checks**: if the project is a satellite, add parent-specific checks (e.g.
  verify inherited files are up to date).
- **Runtime drift**: if the project has a declared runtime, add the specific check.

### 1840-auto-improve

- **Step 3 (Diagnose)**: replace generic commands with:
  - The actual test command (`npm test`, `pytest`, `cargo test`, etc.).
  - The actual build command (`npm run build`, `hugo`, `cargo build`, etc.).
  - The actual lint command (`npm run lint`, `ruff`, `clippy`, etc.).
  - The actual scan command (`npm audit`, `pip-audit`, `trivy`, etc.).
  - Any other project-specific check (e.g. `hugo --gc` for a Hugo site).
- **Step 4 (Plan)**: add project-specific improvement categories:
  - Performance (e.g. Lighthouse for a web site, bench for Rust).
  - Security (e.g. dependency audit, SAST scan).
  - Technical debt (e.g. TODOs, deprecated APIs, code coverage gaps).
  - Documentation (e.g. API docs, README, architecture diagrams).
- **Step 6 (Execute)**: add project-specific protected paths.
- **Step 7 (Verify)**: add project-specific verifications (e.g. smoke test after deploy).

### 1020-handoff

- **Cross-handoff**: if the project has dependencies, personalize the cross-project report
  format.
- **Session bridge**: personalize the default objective derived from the handoff.

### 1040-session-bridge

- **Consumer**: if the project uses a custom consumer instead of `1840-auto-improve`,
  configure the default consumer.
- **Objective derivation**: personalize how the objective is derived from the handoff.

## Flags

- `--dry-run` — produce the report and plan without modifying any files. Verified by clean Git
  status afterward.
- `--focus <csv>` — comma-separated categories: `context`, `rules`, `clients`, `entrypoints`,
  `constitution`. Default is all categories.
- `--refresh-best-practices` — triggers the agent-layer web search to refresh the client
  best-practices cache. Without this flag, the script reads the existing cache (offline).

## Idempotency

Running the analysis twice without changes between runs and without `--refresh-best-practices`
produces the same recommendations (deterministic ordering, no timestamps in recommendation
content). With `--refresh-best-practices`, recommendations may change because external
best-practice sources changed — this is expected, not a bug (DD-009-008).

## Authority boundary

- Never auto-apply changes without human approval.
- Never edit projection files directly — always via canonical sources + `acos --fix`.
- Never remove or rename entrypoints (that's `--reconcile`).
- Never create project-specific entrypoints (that's `1200-metaskill`).
- Preserve user customizations (`managed: false` rules, adopted rules, custom entrypoints,
  project-specific context sections).
- **Never propose a change without referencing the specific file, line, or pattern in the
  actual codebase that justifies it.** Generic recommendations without project-specific
  evidence are rejected.

## Handoff

After Phase 9 is complete, launch `1020-handoff` to persist the session state. This closes the
personalization chain (`0020 → 0040 → 1220-personalize → 1020`). Record in the handoff:
- which entrypoints were personalized (and now carry `personalized: true`)
- which categories were skipped and why
- any remaining personalization gaps for future sessions

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1240-migrate-re.content:
---
description: Dispatch an agent for semantic reference updates after a deterministic ACOS migration
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Treat the user's accompanying text as the migration-reference objective. Minimize questions.

## ⚠️ Autonomy directive — READ BEFORE PROCEEDING

You are an autonomous agent performing semantic reference updates. **You decide, you don't ask.**

- **DO**: Read the referencing files, understand the context of each reference, and decide
  whether it should be `update`, `preserve-verbatim`, or `needs-human-judgment` based on your
  analysis of the surrounding content.
- **DO**: Apply updates for `update` classifications directly. Skip `preserve-verbatim`. Only
  surface `needs-human-judgment` items to the user — and only if you genuinely cannot determine
  the right classification after reading the full context.
- **DO NOT**: Ask the user to confirm each reference update. That is your job — you have the
  rename mapping and the file content, use them.
- **DO NOT**: Surface items as "needs-human-judgment" just because you're unsure. Read more
  context, compare with other references, check the project's conventions — decide.

## Preconditions (operator)

Agent-assisted reference updates are **opt-in**. The migration engine MUST NOT invoke an
agent automatically (REQ-024 / AC-023). Complete the deterministic path first:

1. Run the deterministic migration: `acos-migrate --apply` (or the planned composed apply).
2. Review the reference report: `acos --check --refs-only`.
3. Apply deterministic updates: `acos-migrate --update-refs`.
4. Only then dispatch this entrypoint for remaining **semantic** references.

## Agent dispatch protocol (REQ-042, REQ-025, REQ-053)

When the user dispatches `1240-migrate-refs`, load this payload before editing anything:

1. **Ref report** — the structured report from `acos --check --refs-only` (or an equivalent
   `RefReport` artifact the user attaches). The scanner matches both 3-digit (e.g. `430-migrate`)
   and 4-digit (e.g. `0430-migrate`) visible prefixes, and scans `context-index.md` as a rich
   source of entrypoint references. Treat the in-scope `.ssot/` list as advisory if a
   fresher report is available at dispatch time.
2. **Rename mapping** — the route rename table (`oldPrefix` → `newPrefix`, stable ID, slug).
3. **Referencing file contents** — full text of each file that still has semantic references.
4. **Scope constraint** — modify **only** references to renamed entrypoints. Do not reformat,
   rewrite, or "improve" unrelated prose, structure, or unrelated IDs (REQ-025, INV-009).

### Propagation skill detection (REQ-053)

Before acting, detect a project-specific propagation skill. Glob for any directory matching
`.ssot/skills/acos-propagate-*/` (there should be at most one per project; if several match,
ask the operator which to use). This check runs **before** loading the generic ref-report
payload, because the skill carries the project-specific reference locations, conventions, and
preserve/defer classifications that the generic `.ssot/`-scoped report cannot convey.

#### Path A — propagation skill present

When `.ssot/skills/acos-propagate-<project>/` exists, treat it as the **primary context** and
load it in this order before editing anything:

1. **Router** — read `SKILL.md`. It declares the objective, the pending route, and the
   reference index. Treat it as the authoritative instructions for this dispatch.
2. **Provenance / freshness** — read `provenance.json`. Verify freshness by comparing:
   - `observedState.projectVersion` against the project's current `ssotVersion` (from
     `clients.json`); and
   - `refReportHash` against a freshly recomputed ref report (the skill's own files are
     excluded from the recompute, since they contain entrypoint references by design).

   This check is **advisory, not blocking**. If the skill is stale (version drift or hash
   mismatch), warn the operator:

   > Propagation skill is stale (version changed since generation). Consider regenerating with
   > `acos-migration-generator --with-skill`.

   Then continue using the skill — the operator decides whether to regenerate. Do not refuse
   to proceed.
3. **References** — read, in order:
   - `references/rename-mapping.md` — old→new prefixes, stable IDs, slugs (load first).
   - `references/ref-report.md` — in-scope references under `.ssot/` (advisory snapshot;
     refresh with `acos --check --refs-only` at dispatch time).
   - `references/out-of-scope-locations.md` — references outside the scanner's `.ssot/` root,
     each classified (see below).
   - `references/conventions.md` — how this project formats entrypoint references.
   - `references/protected-paths.md` — paths that MUST NOT be modified.
   - `references/decisions.md` — durable project decisions that may bear on the rename.
4. **Workflow** — load `workflows/propagate.md` and follow it step by step as the primary
   workflow. The generic protocol below (Allowed edits / Forbidden edits) still applies as the
   authority boundary; the skill does not widen write authority (REQ-055).

**Out-of-scope classifications** (from `references/out-of-scope-locations.md`) MUST be
honored explicitly:

- **`update`** — operational reference to a renamed entrypoint. Apply the rename, but present
  the change for explicit human approval before finalizing, because out-of-scope writes are
  outside this entrypoint's default write authority.
- **`preserve-verbatim`** — historical or explanatory reference that intentionally names an
  old prefix. **MUST NOT be modified** (REQ-055). Skip it. Do not "correct" it.
- **`needs-human-judgment`** — ambiguous reference. Present it to the operator with the
  surrounding context and ask how to proceed before making any change.

Do not present the skill's in-scope `.ssot/` payload as a complete accounting of the project's
references; the out-of-scope locations file is the complement that closes the gap.

#### Path B — no propagation skill (fallback)

When no `.ssot/skills/acos-propagate-*/` directory exists, fall back to the generic
ref-report payload:

- Load `.acos/ref-report.json` and `.acos/ref-report-semantic.json` (or the report the
  operator attaches) as the reference set.
- **Warn the operator**:

  > No propagation skill found. Using generic ref-report. Out-of-scope references (root docs,
  > `docs/`) will not be covered.

- Do not present the generic `.ssot/`-scoped payload as a complete accounting of the project's
  references. References outside the scanner's `.ssot/` root were not scanned and must be
  reconciled separately by the operator.
- The generic path has no `preserve-verbatim` / `needs-human-judgment` classifications; apply
  the scope constraint (modify only references to renamed entrypoints) conservatively and flag
  any ambiguous reference for human review.

## Allowed edits

- Update semantic mentions of renamed visible prefixes (both 3-digit forms like `430-migrate`
  and 4-digit forms like `0430-migrate`), stable IDs (when still pointing at the pre-rename
  invocation name in prose), projection paths, and slugs — only where they refer to renamed
  entrypoints from the mapping.
- Prefer the smallest textual change that restores correctness after the rename.

## Forbidden edits

- Changes to lines that do not contain a renamed-entrypoint reference.
- Renames, moves, or content changes outside the attached file set (unless the user explicitly
  approves an out-of-scope update from a propagation skill).
- Invoking further migrations, `acos --fix`, commits, pushes, or destructive cleanup.

## Post-agent diff check (REQ-026)

After edits, run (or ask the operator to run) a line-scope diff check against the pre-agent
baselines:

- For every modified line, verify the line (before and/or after) contains a reference to a
  renamed entrypoint from the mapping.
- Flag any out-of-scope change for human review. Do not merge or continue until those flags are
  resolved.

This check is implemented deterministically by `checkPostAgentLineScope` in
`scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs`: it validates that only lines containing references to
renamed entrypoints were modified, and flags any out-of-scope line change for human review.
When the harness is available, prefer invoking that check rather than a manual diff review.

## Completion report

Report compactly: files touched, reference counts updated, propagation skill used or fallback
warning issued, and any out-of-scope or `preserve-verbatim` items deferred to the human.

---

## Phase 3: Post-merge workflow (when invoked from `1140-migrate-workflow`)

> **Standalone preservation**: This section applies only when `1240-migrate-refs` is invoked as
> Phase 3 of the full hybrid workflow via `1140-migrate-workflow`. The standalone behavior (invoked
> directly for refs-only updates) is unchanged. DD-012: Phase 3 **extends** `1240-migrate-refs` —
> it does not replace it. The standalone path remains available for users who need only semantic
> reference updates without content merging or routing validation.

### Context

When invoked as Phase 3 of the full hybrid workflow, `migration-analysis.json` exists and has been
refined by the agent in Phase 0. The deterministic apply (Phase 2) has already run — entrypoints are
renamed, state files are backfilled, and projections are regenerated. This phase is a **superset** of
the standalone reference-update protocol above: it performs content merging, semantic reference
updates, routing validation, and semantic coherence flagging, then runs the post-agent diff check.

Load `migration-analysis.json` (default path `.ssot/migration-analysis.json`) as the primary
artifact. The analysis contains:

- `renames[].customSections[]` — custom content to merge into renamed files.
- `semanticReferences[]` — semantic references to update (in-scope and out-of-scope).
- `renames[].newSource` — the renamed file path (relative to `.ssot/agents/entrypoints/`).

### Content merge (uses `renames[].customSections[]`)

For each rename in the analysis:

1. Read the renamed file at its new path (`.ssot/agents/entrypoints/<newSource>`).
2. For each `customSection` with a `preservationStrategy`:
   - **`"append"`**: append the custom section content to the end of the renamed file (after the
     template content). Preserve the original heading and body.
   - **`"replace"`**: replace the corresponding template section (matched by heading) with the
     custom content.
   - **`"merge"`**: merge the custom content into the template section (agent judgment on how to
     combine — preserve custom paragraphs while retaining template structure).
3. The custom section content was snapshotted in Phase 1 (`.acos/migrations/snapshots/`). Read
   from there if the original file was already overwritten by the deterministic apply.
4. After merging, verify the file is valid markdown: no broken headings, no duplicate sections,
   no malformed frontmatter.

### Semantic reference updates (uses `semanticReferences[]`)

For each reference in `analysis.semanticReferences[]`:

- **`classification === "update"`**: replace `oldRef` with `newRef` in the file at the specified
  line. Apply the smallest textual change that restores correctness.
- **`classification === "preserve-verbatim"`**: skip — leave as-is. Do not "correct" historical or
  explanatory references (REQ-055).
- **`classification === "needs-human-judgment"`**: present the reference (with surrounding context)
  to the user for a decision before making any change.

Scope rules:

- **In-scope references** (`location === "inScope"`, under `.ssot/`): updated directly within the
  agent's write authority.
- **Out-of-scope references** (`location === "outOfScope"`, elsewhere): require explicit user
  approval per reference before modification. Present each one with context and wait for approval.

### Routing validation

After all content merges and reference updates:

1. Verify that every entrypoint referenced in `workflows.json` exists at its declared `source` path
   under `.ssot/agents/entrypoints/`.
2. Verify that stable IDs are unique across the entrypoints array.
3. Verify that `order` values are unique and multiples of 20 (intermediate lifecycle steps may use
   multiples of 20 between the main groups that use multiples of 20).

Flag any violation for human review before proceeding.

### Semantic incoherence flagging

After merges and reference updates, scan for semantic incoherence and flag for human review:

1. **Stale entrypoint name in custom section**: if a custom section's heading or body references an
   old entrypoint name (prefix/slug) that no longer exists after the rename, flag it.
2. **Incoherent surrounding prose**: if a semantic reference was updated but the surrounding prose
   now reads incoherently (e.g., a sentence that named the old entrypoint now has a dangling
   reference or broken grammar), flag it for human review.
3. **Duplicate content**: if a merged custom section duplicates content already present in the
   template portion of the renamed file, flag it.

Do not auto-resolve incoherence — present each flag with context and let the human decide.

### Projection gap follow-up (spec 012)

After merges, reference updates, and incoherence flagging, follow up on the `preserve-custom`
projection-gap outcomes from Phase 2. The analysis artifact's `projectionGaps` section records which
gaps the agent resolved with `preserve-custom`; the deterministic apply kept those files/entries alive
but they may need explicit registration or semantic validation here.

1. **`orphanedSourceFiles[]` with `resolutionStrategy === "preserve-custom"`**: for each, present the
   file to the operator. If they want it kept as a registered entrypoint (not just a surviving file on
   disk), add a `workflows.json` entry at the next free order ≥600 (reuse the numbering scheme already
   implemented in `analyzeCustomRenumbering`). This is an explicit, human-approved out-of-scope write —
   the same authority pattern used above for `outOfScope` semantic references. If the operator does not
   want it registered, leave the file on disk unregistered (it will not be projected to clients, but it
   is preserved for reference).
2. **`staleEntrypoints[]` with `resolutionStrategy === "preserve-custom"`**: for each, confirm the
   renumbered order (applied deterministically in Phase 2 by `reconcileAgainstTemplate`) still makes
   semantic sense in the post-migration context. If the renumbered order breaks a semantic grouping
   (e.g. a custom entrypoint that was deliberately adjacent to a renamed template entrypoint is now
   far away in the 600+ range), flag it for human review — the operator may want to manually adjust the
   order to a more semantically appropriate slot.

### Surface audit reference follow-up (July 2026 audit)

After projection gap follow-up, check for and correct semantic references related to the new and invalidated surfaces:

1. **Devin `.devin/rules/` as a native CLI surface**: `.devin/rules/` is a native CLI surface — Devin CLI reads `.devin/rules/*.md` natively since v3000.x. Update any documentation that references `.devin/rules/` as a Desktop-only phantom or claims it is not read by the CLI. References describing it as `desktopOnly: true` should be updated to reflect native CLI support.
2. **Codex `.codex/skills/` without legacy note**: update any documentation that references `.codex/skills/` without noting it is legacy (DD-012). `.agents/skills/` is the primary skills location for Codex.
3. **DD-009 and DD-010 references**: check for references to DD-009 (OpenCode has no hooks) or DD-010 (Kilo has no hooks) and update them to note these decisions are invalidated — both clients now have hooks via plugin system (DD-014).
4. **"Kilo has no hooks" / "OpenCode has no hooks"**: search for prose claiming Kilo or OpenCode lack a hooks surface and correct it — both now support hooks via `.kilo/plugin/acos-hooks.ts` and `.opencode/plugins/acos-hooks.ts` respectively.

Each correction is an in-scope semantic reference update if the file is under `.ssot/`; out-of-scope files require explicit user approval per the scope rules above.

### Post-agent diff check (FM-020)

After all modifications, run the post-agent diff check helper to verify scope compliance. Every
modified line must correspond to a `customSection` line range or a `semanticReference` line in the
analysis. Out-of-scope changes are flagged.

Invoke the deterministic check:

```bash
node scripts/core/ssot-migrations.mjs --check-post-agent-diff --root . --analysis .ssot/migration-analysis.json
```

Or call `checkPostAgentDiff(root, analysis)` directly from the harness. The function is read-only
and returns a report:

```json
{
  "inScopeChanges": 12,
  "outOfScopeChanges": 0,
  "outOfScopeFiles": [],
  "outOfScopeLines": [],
  "passed": true
}
```

If `passed === false`, do not proceed to Phase 4. Present the out-of-scope lines to the user for
review and resolution. This extends REQ-026 (post-agent line-scope check) to the hybrid workflow:
the scope is now defined by the analysis artifact rather than a rename-key heuristic.

### Phase 3 completion report

In addition to the standalone completion report above, report:

- Custom sections merged (count per preservation strategy: append/replace/merge).
- Semantic references updated (count), preserved verbatim (count), deferred to human (count).
- Out-of-scope references approved by the user (count).
- Routing validation results (pass/fail with details).
- Semantic incoherence flags raised (count and summary).
- **Projection gaps: N preserved-custom orphans re-registered, N left unregistered (file kept, no workflow entry), N stale entrypoints renumbered.** (spec 012)
- **Surface audit: N references corrected (Devin rules, Codex skills, DD-009/DD-010, Kilo/OpenCode hooks).** (July 2026 audit)
- Post-agent diff check result (`passed`, `outOfScopeChanges`).

Pause for explicit human approval before transitioning to Phase 4 (deterministic verify), per
REQ-069.

## Completion checklist

Before declaring reference updates complete, verify:

- [ ] Propagation skill detected (or fallback warning issued if absent)
- [ ] Rename mapping loaded and verified
- [ ] All `update` classifications applied (show diff for each file)
- [ ] All `preserve-verbatim` items skipped (not modified)
- [ ] All `needs-human-judgment` items presented to user with context
- [ ] Post-agent diff check run (`checkPostAgentLineScope`) — show output
- [ ] No out-of-scope changes (or flagged for human review)
- [ ] Completion report presented with counts (updated, preserved, deferred)

**This entrypoint only updates references.** It does NOT run `acos-migrate --apply`, `acos --fix`,
or any structural migration. If the deterministic migration has not been run yet, stop and route
to `1140-migrate-workflow` first.

---
description: Audit and refresh frontier vs subagent model routing (Anthropic + OpenAI + Cursor) against the canonical matrix
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Treat the user's accompanying text as the model-routing objective. Minimize questions.

## Purpose

Keep **frontier (parent)** and **subagent (execute / verify)** model choices aligned with
`docs/model-selection.md` — quality without burning quota on the wrong tier.

This is **not** the client-surface completeness audit (spec 018 / personalize). That work
updates hooks, permissions, and native files. This entrypoint updates **which model IDs**
belong on which role.

## Canonical combos (as of 2026-10-16)

| Stack | Frontier | Verify / review | Execute / volume |
|-------|----------|-----------------|------------------|
| Anthropic | `claude-opus-5-5` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` (≥ floor) | `claude-haiku-5-5` |
| OpenAI | `gpt-6.1-sol` | Sol (or Luna with care) | `gpt-6-luna` |
| Cursor | Auto / Opus (chat) | ACOS agents `composer-2.5-fast` | Explore `disabled` in `cli-config.json` |

**Banned for new work:** Sonnet 4.6 (dominated by 5.5), Haiku 4.5 (prefer 5.5), Haiku on
planner/reviewer/verifier.

## Procedure

### 1. Deterministic audit

Resolve ACOS root from `clients.json` → `acosSource` (local-checkout or `node_modules/@acos/core`).

```bash
node <acos>/scripts/audit/model-routing-audit.mjs --root <project-root> --json
```

Record hard violations vs warnings. From SSOT **1.9.5**, the audit also checks
`.ssot/agents/clients.json` → `frontierRouting` (consultant / prep / verifyFloor /
forbid / budget). Missing block = warning; invalid verifyFloor or banned models =
hard violation.

### 2. Refresh pricing / IDs (agent)

If the user asked for a refresh, or the audit reports a stale matrix:

1. Fetch current Anthropic + OpenAI pricing / model overview pages.
2. Propose a short diff to `docs/model-selection.md` (and the copy under
   `docs/agent-waves/model-selection.md` if present).
3. **Stop for approval** before editing the canonical doc.

### 3. Apply client overrides (after approval)

Update `.ssot/agents/clients.json` only when the user approved concrete overrides:

- Cursor: `agentModelOverrides` planner/reviewer/verifier → `composer-2.5-fast`
- Claude: keep ACOS agents ≥ `claude-sonnet-5-5`; document Haiku 5.5 for mechanical CLI waves
- Codex: prefer `gpt-6-luna` for volume agents

Then:

```bash
npx --no-install acos --fix
npx --no-install acos --check
node <acos>/scripts/audit/model-routing-audit.mjs --root <project-root>
```

### 4. Cursor machine controls (operator / global)

If Cursor is in scope, verify (do not invent settings keys):

- `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` → `subagentModels.explore: "disabled"`
- `~/.cursor/hooks.json` → `subagentStart` cost guard
- See `docs/agent-waves/13-CURSOR-COST-CONTROLS.md`

### 5. Persist

Update `.ssot/status.md` / `.ssot/handoff.md` with the matrix date and any override changes.
Log durable decisions in `.ssot/decisions.md` when changing default routing policy.

## Authority

- Do **not** lower verifier/reviewer below Sonnet 5.5.
- Do **not** commit credentials or paste API keys from dashboards.
- Multi-project engine refresh: prefer `node <acos>/scripts/lifecycle/acos-rollout.mjs`.

.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1840-auto-impro.content:
---
description: Automated improvement cycle — diagnose, critique, plan, execute, verify, hand off
---

<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:START -->
> **Orientation**: Read `.ssot/context-index.md`, `.ssot/status.md`, and
> `.ssot/handoff.md` before proceeding. Full reference:
> `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md`.
<!-- ACOS-ORIENTATION:END -->

Launch an autonomous auto-improvement cycle on the project. This entrypoint is triggered by
`0020-resume` when it finds `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md`, or directly by the user.

Spec: `docs/specs/019-cycle-continuity/spec.md` — invariants **C1**, **G1**, **H1**, **X1**, **S1**, **B2**, **E1**.

## The chain

```
End of current session:
  1020-handoff         → status.md + handoff.md + S1 scan + H1 hypothesis
  1040-session-bridge  → next-session-prompt.md + snippet (thin)

Next session:
  0020-resume          → consumes prompt → launches 1840-auto-improve
  1840-auto-improve    → diagnose → C1 critique → plan → gate → execute → verify → handoff
```

`0200-frontier-consult` is **optional**. If the user explicitly requests a frontier-model
critique before execution, 1840-auto-improve produces its own plan internally (after C1),
then sends that plan to `0200-frontier-consult` for validation, critique, and improvement.
The frontier model does NOT create the plan from scratch — it reviews and improves the plan
already produced by this entrypoint. Otherwise, 1840-auto-improve produces its own plan
internally and proceeds directly. The frontier-consult path is never the default — it is
opt-in only.

## Inputs

- The user's accompanying text is the **current objective** and may declare a **requested
  phase** (full cycle, analysis-only / transfer, diagnose-only, etc.).
- Intent priority (same as `0020-resume`): current explicit instruction → explicitly active
  resume contract → status/handoff as context. Qualify `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` as
  **absent**, **inactive**, **usable**, or **contradictory** before consuming it. An old or
  inactive bridge must not override a new explicit objective or phase.
- If a **usable** bridge is selected under that priority, read the **whole** file (Objective,
  Hypothesis, Constraints, Context, Waves, Sub-agents) — not the objective line alone. Waves
  and Sub-agents are a rendering of H1. Critique them in C1; do not execute them as written.
- Prior hypothesis (H1): `.session/next-cycle-hypothesis.md` or alias
  `.session/next-cycle-analysis.md` (search order: hypothesis → analysis → handoff-only
  degraded). Missing or inactive H1 is allowed for a first cycle; C1 records
  `degraded_input: true`.
- `--from-frontier` (optional) — indicates a frontier-model critique already exists at the
  `planConsumer.specPath`/`planFile` location. The internal plan was produced, sent to the
  frontier model for critique, and the improved plan was written back. Read the improved plan
  and skip re-planning. This flag is only set when `0200-frontier-consult --consumer
  1840-auto-improve` was invoked after the internal plan was produced.
- `--frontier` (optional) — explicitly request a frontier-model critique of the internal plan
  before execution. Produce diagnose + C1 + internal plan first, then invoke
  `0200-frontier-consult --consumer 1840-auto-improve`. After the frontier model improves the
  plan, continue with `--from-frontier` semantics. The only approval remains G1.

## Procedure

1. **Read the cycle contract** — apply intent priority. Prefer the current explicit user
   instruction for objective and requested phase. If a usable bridge is selected and not
   contradicted, read the whole file as context/contract. Also read H1 if present (qualify
   inactive sentinels). If neither provides a clear objective, ask the user what they want
   to improve. Record the requested phase: full execute (default) vs **analysis-only /
   transfer** (stop after artifacts; no implementation, commit, or implicit relaunch).

2. **Frontier-consult gate (optional)** — if `--frontier` was provided OR the user
   explicitly asks for a frontier-model critique:
   - **Produce diagnose + C1 + internal plan first** (steps 3–5 below), then return here.
   - Launch `0200-frontier-consult --consumer 1840-auto-improve` with the objective AND
     the full evidence bundle as context — paths to `.session/diagnostic.md`,
     `.session/hypothesis-critique.md`, `.session/plan.md` (the internal plan), and the
     H1 artifact if present. The frontier model validates, critiques, and improves the
     plan against that evidence — it does NOT create one from scratch.
   - After the frontier model returns the improved plan, continue with
     `--from-frontier` semantics (the improved plan file is pre-existing). The only
     approval is the human gate (G1). Do not ask for a separate frontier approval.
   - If the user did NOT request frontier-consult, skip this step entirely and use the
     internal plan directly (step 5).

3. **Diagnose the real state** — run the project's standard verification commands to
   establish a baseline. This is project-specific and SHOULD be personalized by the
   `1220-personalize` skill. Two modes:

   **Single-project mode** (default — standalone project or satellite):
   - Read `AGENTS.md` for the project's operating contract, build/test commands, and
     conventions. Verify that the Build, Test, Conventions, and Boundaries sections are
     populated and match the actual codebase. If `AGENTS.md` still contains placeholder
     text (`_Run 1220-personalize to populate..._`) or references stale commands, flag
     this as a personalization gap and add "run `1220-personalize`" to the improvement
     plan.
   - Read `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md` for the last known state.
   - Run the project's test suite (detect the framework: `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test`,
     `cargo test`, etc.).
   - Run the project's build (detect: `npm run build`, `hugo`, `cargo build`, etc.).
   - Run `npx --no-install acos --check` to verify SSOT projection sync.
   - Run `git status` to detect uncommitted changes.
   - If the project has a lint command, run it.
   - If the project has a secrets-scan command, run it.
   - Record the diagnostic results in `.session/diagnostic.md`.
   - **Research before asking**: when the diagnosis reveals ambiguities or unknowns,
     resolve them through codebase exploration, documentation, or web research (rule 8)
     before surfacing them to the user. Only ask the user as a last resort, with structured
     options and justified recommendations.
   - If tests or build fail: the cycle becomes a **correction cycle**, not an improvement
     cycle. Prioritize fixing the failures before any improvement work.

   **Ecosystem mode** (container with `ecosystemChildren` — when the objective spans
   multiple satellites or the container itself):
   - Read `specs/ecosystem-integration/capability-evidence.json` if it exists, to establish
     the current proof-level baseline.
   - Launch N sub-agents in parallel (one per relevant satellite, max 5 concurrent):
     each sub-agent reads `<satellite>/.ssot/status.md` + `handoff.md`, runs the
     satellite's test suite, and returns a compact diagnostic (tests pass/fail count,
     last commit SHA, open blockers). Sub-agents re-orient independently per
     `orientation.md` → "When you are a sub-agent".
   - The parent agent aggregates all sub-agent diagnostics into `.session/diagnostic.md`
     with a per-satellite table.
   - If the diagnostic reveals a need for wave decomposition (multi-satellite,
     multi-domain work), invoke `0160-wave-plan-prep` as a **child prep** (parent-owned):
     it returns `wave-prep.md` to this entrypoint without a second user gate. The single
     **G1** remains step 6 on the complete plan.
   - If tests or build fail on any satellite: that satellite becomes a **correction
     priority** in the plan.

4. **C1 — Critique the previous hypothesis (mandatory)** — write
   `.session/hypothesis-critique.md` **before** planning or the human gate.

   For each material claim or candidate lane in H1 (or, if H1 is missing, from handoff +
   prompt — mark `degraded_input: true`):

   | Field | Meaning |
   |-------|---------|
   | `claim` | What session N asserted or proposed |
   | `live_check` | What was re-verified this session |
   | `verdict` | `keep` \| `amend` \| `drop` \| `blocked` |
   | `enrichment` | What to add or correct for the plan |
   | `evidence` | Path, command, or observation |

   Rules:
   - Prefer live evidence over prior narrative (**autocritique**).
   - Do not copy H1 unchanged into the plan. At least one amend/drop/enrichment **or**
     explicit "all keep" with revalidation evidence is required.
   - Do not present the human gate until this file exists.

5. **Plan** — produce a **single recommended** plan in `.session/plan.md` derived from C1
   (not a menu of peer strategies):
   - If `--from-frontier` was set: read the improved plan from
     `<specPath>/<planFile>` (declared in the `planConsumer` frontmatter) and use it
     directly. Skip internal planning — the plan was already produced internally and
     improved by the frontier model.
   - Otherwise: based on diagnostic + C1, identify what to do:
     - **If things are green**: identify improvements (design, performance, security,
       technical debt, UX, missing tests, documentation gaps). Prioritize by impact.
     - **If things are red**: identify the corrections needed. Prioritize by severity.
   - **Cycle substance (mandatory)** — a cycle is analysis plus material
     improvements, enrichments, or corrections. It is **not** a wrapper for a routine
     micro-edit. Forbidden as the sole deliverable of a cycle: a one- or two-line tweak,
     a typo/comment-only change, or a single trivial task that belongs to an ordinary
     agent turn outside the cycle. Each planned task MUST state why it is cycle-worthy
     (expected impact / multi-concern or multi-file scope / high-impact justification).
     If diagnose + C1 find only trivial work: either expand into a related substantive
     package, or **stop** and report that no cycle-worthy work remains — do not invent
     busywork and do not run a hollow cycle.
   - **Standard mode** (≤5 tasks, single project): break into prioritized tasks
     (max 5 per cycle to keep the scope bounded). Each task must have: description,
     files affected, domain (code|tests|docs|infra), dependencies, a verification
     command, and a one-line cycle-worthiness rationale.
   - **Wave mode** (>5 tasks OR multi-satellite OR diagnostic invoked
     `0160-wave-plan-prep`): decompose into waves following the agent-wave orchestration
     pattern (diagnose → fix → validate → ship):
     - Wave 1 = diagnose (parallel across lanes / projects when read-only and
       ownership-disjoint, including **within a single repository**)
     - Wave 2 = fix/implement (parallel across ownership-disjoint write-sets in the
       same repository or across satellites; serialize only overlapping files,
       shared generation, or true dependencies)
     - Wave 3 = validate (sequential integration barrier)
     - Wave 4 = ship/handoff (sequential)
     - Structure: resolve the active feature directory via artifact path resolution
       (explicit path → project-declared active source → `docs/specs/<id>` then
       `specs/<id>`; default consumer path remains `specs/`). Prefer reusing an
       existing package (e.g. `docs/specs/021-…`) over re-deriving tasks. Write
       `waves/manifest.json` with per-lane `promptFile`, `reportFile`, `statusFile`.
     - Each task must have: description, files affected, domain, dependencies,
       verification command, `Parallelizable: true|false`, `Lane` assignment.
     - Max 5 parallel lanes per wave (coordination cost). Example: six file-disjoint
       tasks in one repo may run as parallel lanes when write-sets do not overlap.
     - **Shared generation** (projection regeneration, pack-wide sync, shared manifests)
       is reserved for the **coordinator / parent** after lane barriers — not for
       concurrent lane agents.
     - Child `0160-wave-plan-prep` returns prep only; it does not hold a second G1.

6. **Human gate (G1)** — present **one** recommended plan to the user, backed by the
   analysis that produced it. Wait for approval before executing. Do NOT execute blindly.
   This is the **single** human gate in the cycle (parent-owned). Child prep (`0160`)
   and sub-agent lanes do not present additional Approve/Amend gates.
   - Required presentation: (a) the preliminary analysis — the viable options considered
     and the impact / trade-offs of each, including options rejected during diagnose + C1;
     (b) the recommended plan from `.session/plan.md` as a **concrete file-by-file /
     task-by-task list** (what changes, in which paths — not abstract option letters),
     with a short justification (why this option, what C1 kept / amended / dropped);
     (c) the semantic outcomes **Approve** or **Amend** (user specifies changes).
   - Deliver the gate through the client's structured-choice surface when one exists —
     on Cursor that is the **AskQuestion** tool (question tool, menus, buttons).
     **Approve** is the identified recommendation, answerable in one click; **Amend**
     collects the user's changes via the surface's fallback path (e.g. "Other").
   - **Forbidden gate UX**: asking the user to type free-form answers such as
     "approve", "disapprove", "reject", "amend", or option numbers when a
     structured-choice surface exists. That is an open-text prompt — a G1 violation
     (rule 9). If AskQuestion / the surface is unavailable in the current model
     session, say so in one sentence, still present the concrete recommended plan,
     and use the shortest possible confirmation path — never a multi-paragraph
     typed quiz.
   - Alternatives are **analysis, not a menu**: each is shown with its impact and why it
     was kept or rejected. "No menus" forbids co-equal options without a recommendation —
     it does NOT forbid showing the decision space (rule 9).
   - If the user amends, update `.session/plan.md` accordingly.
   - **Forbidden**: multi-choice menus such as Approve B1 / Skip B1 / Reject cycle as peer
     defaults; a bare plan with no analysis of alternatives; asking the user to invent
     the plan when diagnose+C1 already produced one.
   - Edge case only: if the user refuses the objective entirely, stop and ask for a new
     objective — this is not a routine menu option.
   - **Analysis-only / transfer phase**: after diagnostic, C1, plan (and tasks / wave-prep
     as needed) exist as concrete artifacts, **stop**. Do not run step 7 execute, do not
     commit, do not push, do not implicitly relaunch the next cycle. Hand off the
     artifacts and remaining G1/execute decision to the operator or next session.
     Analysis-only is **not** execute authorization. **X1** still applies: do not delete
     `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` here.

7. **Execute** — implement the approved tasks (skip entirely when requested phase is
   analysis-only / transfer). Two modes:

   **Standard mode** (≤5 tasks, single project):
   - Implement tasks one by one or in parallel if independent (ownership-disjoint
     write-sets).
   - Respect protected paths (`protected-paths.json`).
   - Respect the constitution and existing decisions (`.ssot/decisions.md`).
   - Do not invent features outside the active spec.
   - Preserve unrelated changes in the working tree.
   - After each task, run its verification command. If it fails, fix before continuing
     to the next task.

   **Wave mode** (>5 tasks OR multi-satellite OR ownership-disjoint lanes in one repo):
   - For each wave (diagnose → fix → validate → ship):
     - Launch N sub-agents in parallel (one per lane/task, max 5 concurrent) when
       write-sets are file-disjoint — **including six disjoint tasks in a single
       repository**. All parallel sub-agents for one wave MUST be dispatched in a
       single message to achieve true parallelism.
     - **File-disjoint only**: before dispatching, list the files each task will touch.
       If two tasks touch the same file (or overlapping globs/dirs conservatively),
       run them sequentially in the same subagent. Parallel writes to one file corrupt work.
     - Shared projection generation and other shared outputs stay with the coordinator
       parent after the wave barrier — lanes do not regenerate projections.
     - Each sub-agent prompt must include: task ID, exact file paths it may
       create/modify (the disjoint set), files it may read but not write (context),
       acceptance criteria, and "Do not touch files outside your allowed set."
     - Sub-agents re-orient independently per `orientation.md` → "When you are a
       sub-agent" — they do NOT share the calling agent's context.
     - Wait for all sub-agents to return before proceeding to the next wave.
     - If any sub-agent reports `blocked`: launch a targeted fix wave (max 3 cycles),
       then escalate to the user.
   - After each wave, the parent agent runs the relevant verification commands
     (never trust sub-agent-reported pass without re-running).

8. **Verify** — re-run the same verification commands as step 3. If regressions appear,
   fix them before continuing. Record results in `.session/verify.md`.

9. **Handoff** — ensure the **S1** scan artifacts and an H1 draft are ready (or
   let `1020` run the parallel scan and write it), then launch `1020-handoff`
   to close the session:
   - Update `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md`.
   - Run / let `1020` run the parallel next-cycle scan (**S1**) into
     `.session/next-cycle-scan/` — mandatory after a `1840` cycle.
   - Write/refresh `.session/next-cycle-hypothesis.md` (**H1**), citing the
     scan artifacts, before `1040`. H1 candidate lanes MUST meet the cycle
     substance bar (step 5) — micro-edits are non-goals or routine work, not lanes.
   - Record decisions in `.ssot/decisions.md`.
   - Sync the SSOT (`0660-sync`).
   - Commit the changes (do not push without explicit authorization).
   - `1020` invokes `1040-session-bridge` mandatorily.
   - **Close incomplete without B2 + briefing**: the cycle is not finished until
     `1040` has written `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` and the agent has shown the
     user (1) the **plain-language close-briefing skeleton** from `1040` step 8
     (one sentence + numbered tasks + waves + sub-agents + invite to change now),
     then (2) the resume snippet inside a markdown **fenced code block** (and
     attempted clipboard copy). Ending with a bare snippet, opaque jargon, or a
     single incomprehensible sentence instead of that skeleton is a cycle failure.

10. **Cleanup (X1)** — `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` is the cycle contract: it stays
    on disk for the whole cycle so the objective and constraints remain referenceable
    and an interrupted session can be re-launched. Nobody deletes it at cycle start —
    not `0020`, not this entrypoint. The consumed prompt is deleted only at the end,
    inside `1040-session-bridge` (invoked during step 9): `1040` removes the consumed
    prompt **immediately before** writing the **new** prompt for the next session.
    Do **not** delete
    `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` after `1040` writes the **new** prompt —
    that file belongs to the next session. If the cycle ends without `1040`
    writing a replacement (abort, gate refusal, interruption), the previous prompt
    stays in place: the next `0020` launches it again and C1 revalidates it —
    or the user can delete it / re-run `1040-session-bridge` manually.

## Personalization

This entrypoint is project-agnostic in ACOS core. The `1220-personalize` skill SHOULD
specialize it for each project by:
- Replacing the generic diagnostic commands (step 3) with the project's actual test,
  build, lint, and scan commands.
- Adding project-specific protected paths and constraints to step 7.
- Adding project-specific improvement categories to step 5.
- Adding project-specific verification requirements to step 8.

Personalization MUST NOT remove C1/G1/H1/X1 or replace the gate with a skip/reject menu.

The personalized version lives in the project's `.ssot/agents/entrypoints/1840-auto-improve.md`
and overrides the ACOS template version.

## Reminders

- Autocritique is mandatory: never trust the previous agent's claims without live
  revalidation (C1).
- The cycle does NOT relaunch automatically. Wait for human validation at the gate.
- If the diagnostic reveals a blocker (P0, external ops, human action), stop and report it.
- Do NOT push to the remote without explicit authorization.
- Do NOT deploy without explicit authorization.
- If the conversation context becomes long, launch `1060-compact` before execution.
- `0200-frontier-consult` is optional and opt-in only. The default path is internal
  planning. When `--frontier` is used, the frontier model critiques and improves the
  internal plan — it does NOT create a plan from scratch. Never invoke frontier-consult
  without an explicit user request or `--frontier` flag.

## Authority

- This entrypoint has **bounded autonomy**: it reads, writes code, runs tests, and commits,
  but does not push or deploy.
- C1 and the human gate (G1) are mandatory. No execution without approve/amend.
- The handoff at step 9 is mandatory. No session ends without a handoff + H1 path to 1040.

## planConsumer (optional — only used when --frontier is set)

```yaml
planConsumer:
  specPath: "specs/auto-improve-{date}/"
  planFile: "tasks.md"
  planFormat: |
    - [ ] **T-001** — <description>
      - Depends on: none
      - Files: `<path>`
      - Domain: code|tests|docs|infra
      - Parallelizable: true|false
      - Lane: A1
```

This section is only read by `0200-frontier-consult` when `--consumer 1840-auto-improve` is
invoked (after the internal plan is produced). It has no effect on the default (internal
planning) path. The frontier model receives the internal plan as context and returns an
improved version in this format.
